💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wow, this is a nasty, dirty, polluting stunner I didn’t see until just now.
  • In a recent development, anthropic, the AI tech giant behind Claude, has reportedly signed a $3.4 billion contract to buy gas-fired engines (power plants) from OnePWR Solutions, a Texas-based energy company.
  • If you thought Anthropic was supposed to be “the good guy” in the AI industry, perhaps think again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wow, this is a nasty, dirty, polluting stunner I didn’t see until just now.

In a recent development, anthropic, the AI tech giant behind Claude, has reportedly signed a $3.4 billion contract to buy gas-fired engines (power plants) from OnePWR Solutions, a Texas-based energy company. These gas power plants would be able to provide Anthropic’s AI data centers with an enormous amount of off-grid electricity — with the real cost being an enormous amount of air pollution and global warming emissions.

If you thought Anthropic was supposed to be “the good guy” in the AI industry, perhaps think again.

According to recent reports, the Financial Times, which broke the news on this, says that this is the “largest known single purchase of power-generation equipment by an AI lab.” It’s this line from Futurism that really sums up my feelings: “It isn’t just symptomatic of a desperate race to secure the necessary utilities: it’s also one of the clearest signs yet that the AI industry has turned its back on the growing climate crisis in favor of pollution-spewing gas generators it’s installing across the globe.” Indeed. It’s one thing to be racing to be a leader in this field, but to turn to polluting, climate-destroying gas power plants instead of solar and wind power, that’s absolutely disappointing and — frankly — morally disgusting.

For the heck of it, to see what this firm’s AI bot thought about the power choice it made, I decided to ask Claude “Are gas power plants harmful to our climate?” The response was as follows:.

“Yes, though they’re less harmful than coal and more harmful than most alternatives.

“The climate cost has two parts:.

Sources indicate that “Bottom line: Gas is a cleaner fossil fuel, not a clean one. Its climate impact is best judged by what it replaces (coal vs. renewables) and by how tightly methane leaks are controlled. Carbon capture could reduce plant emissions, but it’s still costly and not widely deployed.”.

So, yeah, when you’re choosing to buy $3.4 billion worth of gas power plants instead of renewable energy power plants, that is without a doubt going to be a horrible decision for our climate. I’m sure if I asked Claude about the risk humans race from climate change, the answer would not be uplifting. But I’m not going to go there. Instead, I’ll turn back to Futurism for this summary: “Researchers have found that the effects of AI on the environment are nothing short of devastating. And the prognosis for the future is grim. Last month, environmental nonprofit Sierra Club estimated that upcoming AI data centers could release 2.1 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide by 2030, wiping out nearly 15 years worth of greenhouse gas reduction efforts.”.

Industry observers note that indeed — we’re facing drastic increases in emissions from the very dirty AI industry. The good news is people are already showing they’re fed up with AI data centers. Apparently, out of 41 ballot measures related to data centers that were up for a vote in the recent midterm elections, only one (1) went the way of the AI industry. That said, I don’t see investments in growth stopping right now, as is evidenced by this $3.4 billion gas engine order and OpenAI and others burning through billions of dollars a quarter.

The Largest Hummer In The World Has Two Stories And A Full Kitchen

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Humans can get very creative when it comes to cars.
  • Recent findings suggest that well, you'll probably end up with something like this: a Hummer H1 that's two stories high, about the length of a large city bus, and as wide as an average residential swimming pool.
  • Inside, you're probably expecting a seat big enough for King Kong, and even a space for him to have a foot spa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Humans can get very creative when it comes to cars. Take well-known French artist Benedetto Bufalino, for instance, who once turned a Ford Mondeo wagon into a pizza oven. Then there's the Ohio resident who transformed an E-One fire engine into a mobile pub, because why the heck not? Both are fabulous ideas, and certainly worthy of applause, but what happens when you crank the ambition bar up a few more notches?

Recent findings suggest that well, you'll probably end up with something like this: a Hummer H1 that's two stories high, about the length of a large city bus, and as wide as an average residential swimming pool. Dubbed the X3, it is said to be three times the size of a standard H1, which is already major enough to embarrass the largest production cars ever made. Oh, and at over 130,000 pounds, it's also heavier than a sperm whale.

Inside, you're probably expecting a seat big enough for King Kong, and even a space for him to have a foot spa. Well, that's probably a little too ambitious, but not that far off. You see, the X3 has two floors, and between them there's a lounge, kitchen, and an all-key restroom. This takes the definition of a "man cave" to whole fresh heights — no pun intended.

The X3 is the brainchild of Emirati billionaire and recognized car enthusiast Hamad Al Nahyan, also fondly known as the Rainbow Sheikh. He owns one of the largest car collections in the world, mainly consisting of a multitude of bizarre one-off cars, and so is probably the only person crazy enough to conceive something like the X3. It also took a crew of seven around 1.5 years to build.

Industry observers note that access is granted by a retractable staircase located under its body, because imagine trying to haul the door open — that would be pretty difficult even for an army of Arnold Schwarzeneggers, let alone the average human. Climbing up to the first floor, you're greeted by a fully furnished kitchen area with a (presumably) running sink and wood-lined panels. The door to its left opens up into the toilet area, while opposite are the engine room (more on that below) and the stairs heading up to the second floor.

This magnificent 645-square-foot space has 10 comfortable-looking chairs, with panoramic views all around thanks to the humongous windows, and blinds to black out the cabin if a spot of privacy is needed. The driver's cockpit sits at the back of this floor, featuring all manner of buttons that do ... something. There's no conventional steering wheel either, because the vehicle is controlled using a joystick. And to help see beyond its substantial dimensions, there are live camera feeds giving you a view of the outside world.

A LARC-LX from the U.S. Army fleet, to be precise. It was an amphibious cargo vehicle that did a lot of the gritty work, so the X3 retains its steel hull frame. The one room we're yet to talk about is the engine room: within it sits a quartet of diesel engines, each responsible for powering its own wheel. The wheels are substantial enough to swallow a human whole (and then some), and the tires supposedly cost $25,000 a pop. The total power output is a staggering 1,000 hp. No surprises there, given how much weight it's moving. Top speed is just 20 mph, again for obvious reasons.

According to recent reports, you get a real feel for just how major this thing is when you look at the details, too. Apparently, you need a crane to get beneath the hood, and the X3 also has what seem to be the world's largest windshield wipers. Despite all this, it can actually be driven on public roads, albeit with a police escort, and since this is the Middle East we're talking about, stated police cars are probably Ferraris, Lamborghinis, Bugattis, and other dream exotics. So, reckon this is the ultimate zombie apocalypse hideout?

The Best Rental Car Companies In 2026 According To JD Power

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that many auto dealerships have a well-earned reputation for making life difficult for customers, but it doesn't always get easier trying to rent.
  • In a recent development, according to the JD Power 2026 North America Rental Car Satisfaction Study, overall customer satisfaction saw some notable improvements over 2025 — especially in two key areas.
  • As for what goes into the results, JD Power bases them on ease of rental, pick-up/drop-off, level of trust, vehicle, staff, value for price paid, and digital tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that many auto dealerships have a well-earned reputation for making life difficult for customers, but it doesn't always get easier trying to rent. Whether they're charging customers for breaking the laws of physics or relying on AI scanners to bill $440 for a wheel scuff, rental car agencies obviously have some work to do when it comes to boosting customer satisfaction. The good news is that that seems to be happening.

In a recent development, according to the JD Power 2026 North America Rental Car Satisfaction Study, overall customer satisfaction saw some notable improvements over 2025 — especially in two key areas. First, 90% of rental car customers said that, when they arrived at the counter, a vehicle from the class they reserved was waiting for them. That is, they reserved a mid-size sedan and one was there. Getting a bit more detailed, 85% claimed they "were able to pick a specific vehicle within the class they were given." Those figures were up 3 and 5 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, the study's average satisfaction score went from 691 in 2025 — on a 1,000-point scale — to 707 this year.

As for what goes into the results, JD Power bases them on ease of rental, pick-up/drop-off, level of trust, vehicle, staff, value for price paid, and digital tools. Those seven "core dimensions" are then weighted in the order they're listed. The outcome for 2026 was that six of 13 agencies finished with above-average scores, led by Enterprise, National, Advantage Rent A Car, Alamo, Sixt, and Hertz. Bringing up the rear were Thrifty and Dollar. Finally, all this data comes from 7,845 survey respondents, all of whom had rented their cars from airport-based rental companies in the span between August 2025 and August 2026.

According to recent reports, it's worth pointing out that all 13 rental agencies earned higher study scores this year than last, with a lot of that improvement coming at the lower levels. Dollar, for instance, was at the very bottom of the rankings for both 2025 and 2026, yet its score jumped from 641 to 663. The biggest advance in terms of points was for Payless — it went from 11th place with 650 points last year to 8th place with 699 points this time around.

It has been revealed that the standings didn't change much at the other end of the spectrum, though. The order remained the same, with Enterprise setting the pace, followed by National and Advantage Rent A Car, and they each saw essentially the same improvements: Enterprise was up 5 points to 739, National improved the same amount to 726 points, and Advantage advanced 6 points, rising from 711 to 717. (Technically, Advantage was tied with Sixt in 2025. Despite a three-point bump in its satisfaction score, that last agency slipped to fifth place in 2026, falling behind Alamo's 716 points.).

Oh, and there's one other factoid you should keep in mind about the rental car agencies: every major rental car brand in the country is owned by one of three companies.

Enterprise Mobility owns Enterprise, of course, but it has National and Alamo under its umbrella as well. Likewise, Avis Budget Group controls its namesake rental brands plus Payless, and Hertz has its own trio that extends to Dollar and Thrifty. Hertz also had purchased Advantage and owned that brand for a time. It's just that when Hertz bought Dollar and Thrifty in 2012, the FTC forced Hertz to sell off Advantage to maintain a competitive market.

Breaking: What The US Midterm Elections Mean For Climate Progress

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • People across the United States voted in record numbers in last week’s incredibly consequential election, which has completely changed the makeup of Congress for its new term beginning in January 2027.
  • Will the Trump administration acknowledge voters’ repudiation of its destructive agenda and work in cooperation with this new Congress?
  • Sources indicate that energy affordability concerns, opposition to proliferating data centers, and anger at corruption and extreme economic inequality were undoubtedly driving forces in how people voted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

People across the United States voted in record numbers in last week’s incredibly consequential election, which has completely changed the makeup of Congress for its new term beginning in January 2027. The success of our electoral processes—still underway—should not be taken for granted. It’s a win for democracy when millions of citizens peacefully claim their right to a government of, by, and for the people.

Will the Trump administration acknowledge voters’ repudiation of its destructive agenda and work in cooperation with this new Congress? That remains to be seen, and I’m not holding my breath. But there’s no question that the shift in Congress has significant implications for the administration’s ability to continue to ram through its anti-science, authoritarian agenda—including on climate and clean energy issues.

Sources indicate that energy affordability concerns, opposition to proliferating data centers, and anger at corruption and extreme economic inequality were undoubtedly driving forces in how people voted. While not everyone explicitly named climate change as a top issue (although many did put it in their top three), its fingerprints are all over the concerns a majority of voters did name in polls.

If you care about addressing the high costs of electricity and gas, then you must reckon with the fact that this current fossil energy crisis, unleashed by the Trump administration’s war against Iran, is an extreme manifestation of the risks of fossil fuel dependence. The benefits of a transition away from fossil fuels to renewable energy—renewable energy that the Trump administration has relentlessly attacked, further driving up costs for consumers—are tremendous. If you are deeply concerned about the rapid, unregulated build-out of data centers, you know that it comes with huge risks for communities related to climate, water, pollution, health, and electricity cost burdens. And it’s so clear that the Trump administration’s corruption, lies about climate science, and massive giveaways to fossil fuel polluters are leaving us all bearing the high costs of climate damages while large corporations and the president’s inner circle are raking in enormous profits.

Here’s another reality: regardless of politics, climate change is here, and science shows it’s rapidly worsening with the world’s imminent overshoot of 1.5°C of global warming. Communities are already experiencing deadly and costly climate impacts, including extreme heatwaves, catastrophic wildfires, record-breaking flooding, drought, accelerating sea level rise, intense ocean heat, irreversible loss of glaciers and ice sheets, stresses to critical ecosystems and more. These impacts are showing up in people’s daily lives—harming their health, destroying homes, livelihoods, and critical infrastructure, raising insurance premiums, hammering businesses, stressing water supplies, and threatening food security and affordability.

According to recent reports, climate change and clean energy are pocketbook complications. They are a lot more than that, of course. And climate change does not care if you live in a red state or a blue state. (One can ask if that is that even a relevant frame after an election that scrambled all conventional wisdom about “red” and “blue” dichotomies.).

It has been revealed that importantly, we will soon have a Congress where a majority accepts the scientific evidence on climate change. (Yes, I also wish we could take that for granted in 2026, but not in US politics, sadly.) That’s an crucial start and means we can advocate for policymakers to legislate based on the facts, instead of being stuck fighting disinformation and lies.

Here’s what this seismic “change election” could mean for action on climate change, some cautions about what likely won’t change right away, and what we’ll have to keep fighting for.

We will have to keep fighting back in courts to hold the Trump administration accountable for egregiously flouting the law. We’ve already had a major win in a lawsuit where the administration was found to be violating the Federal Advisory Committee Act in secretly setting up a ‘Climate Working Group’ stacked with climate contrarians to draft a sham science report, which the EPA then used to justify its proposal to gut the Endangerment Finding. We’ve also filed suit against the administration for repealing the Endangerment Finding, contrary to law, science, and the public interest.

It has been revealed that on the international front, the Trump administration has shamefully exited the bedrock UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement, and that won’t change as long as it is in power. As I write from COP31 in Türkiye, the administration’s abandonment of global climate cooperation is very much on my mind; it’s crucial for the rest of the world to forge ahead regardless of the high stakes. There is a real risk that a beleaguered Trump administration will double down on its authoritarian ways and continue to find new ways to disrupt global climate progress and multilateral institutions. But Congress now has the power and responsibility to keep this reckless administration in check and ensure it is held accountable, at home and on the global stage.

“Change elections” come weighted with the hopes and dreams of many. As climate justice advocates, we know that policymakers have pushed off meaningful climate action far too long, and those failures are putting us all at profound risk. Yet, deep-pocketed fossil fuel interests, Substantial Tech, and other powerful entities continue to obstruct and delay action, still hold all too much sway over both parties in Congress, and we can expect their harmful tactics to ratchet up. So now it’s our responsibility to fight for what comes next, to make our shared dreams come true. Because those dreams of a safer, more just world for generations of young people to come must become reality.

Courtesy of The Equation, USC, by Rachel Cleetus.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roanoke City Schools to Add 313 kW Solar Power System.

Sources indicate that staunton, VA — Secure Solar Futures, a provider of on-site clean energy to schools, local governments, and businesses, will build a 313-kilowatt solar power system installed at Preston Park Elementary School in Roanoke, VA. Construction of the system is expected later this year at no capital cost to the Roanoke Schools through a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement with Secure Solar Futures. Pardee Renewable Energy LLC, a subsidiary of Pardee Resources Company, will provide the majority of the capital for the solar system.

A total of 531 bi-facial solar panels manufactured by VSUN Solar in Houston, TX, will be installed on the rooftop of the school located at 3142 Preston Avenue, NW, and will offset 67% of the power used by the school annually.

In its first year, the school’s solar system will produce 421 megawatt hours of clean energy, enough to power 44 average Virginia homes and provide environmental benefits by avoiding 371 metric tons of carbon pollution, which is equal to the emissions produced by 87 gasoline-powered passenger vehicles, or the carbon sequestered by 372 acres of U.S. forests, according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

Under the Power Purchase Agreement, the solar power equipment will be provided at no upfront cost to Roanoke Schools. For the 25-year term of the agreement, Pardee Renewable Energy LLC, together with its partner Secure Solar Futures, will own, operate, and maintain the solar power system and will sell the energy produced to the school division at a rate lower than the local electric utility.

During the term of the Power Purchase Agreement, Preston Park Elementary School will save $581,000 in net avoided costs for electricity. After the conclusion of the term, Roanoke Schools can opt to take ownership of the solar power system at a nominal cost, producing its own energy for the remainder of the equipment’s 35- to 40-year productive lifespan.

About Roanoke City Public Schools.

In a recent development, roanoke City Public Schools (RCPS) is an urban school division in Roanoke, Virginia, serving a pre-K through 12th grade population of approximately 14,000 students. RCPS provides an inclusive and equitable, student-centered culture that empowers lifelong learning. Through meaningful, relevant, and engaging learning opportunities, we will empower all students to dream, excel, and meet their full potential to benefit our city and its citizens. The division has 17 elementary schools, five middle schools, two high schools, and five program locations, including the Roanoke Valley Governor’s School for Science & Technology and two career and technical education centers. Visit www.rcps.info for additional information.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's no arguing that the people of the city of Detroit tend to keep things interesting.
  • Williams was one of the two men involved in the horse-meets-bus adventure.
  • At one point you hear the amused bus driver mention something about the horses being service animals, and Williams responding with a joking "yup." The driver then lowered a ramp that would allow the horses to more easily walk aboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's no arguing that the people of the city of Detroit tend to keep things interesting. Earlier this year, a priest punched the fear of God into a fleeing teen driver after a crash. The latest stunt to capture the nation's attention was two young Detroit men taking their horses onto a city bus. The outing was Raven's first time in the major city, according to the Detroit Free Press. Raven is one of 12 horses Jordan Williams uses as part of his Urban City Cowboys program: a Western rodeo school outside of Detroit, as well as an organization that offers equestrian therapy to children with disabilities.

Williams was one of the two men involved in the horse-meets-bus adventure. The other was a close friend who had come along with his horse for a fundraiser earlier in the day. While riding near 7 Mile Road, they had stopped near a Detroit Department of Transportation bus stop. One of the buses had also stopped for them and the driver asked if they wanted on. If you listen to the video circulating the internet compiled from the cameras on the DDOT bus, you can hear the driver say to Williams and his friend, "If they can get in here, it is what it is.".

At one point you hear the amused bus driver mention something about the horses being service animals, and Williams responding with a joking "yup." The driver then lowered a ramp that would allow the horses to more easily walk aboard. Sure enough, both Raven and the other horse entered the bus with the men, trotted down the aisle, and exited from the rear side exit as the automated greeting told the horses, "Welcome aboard." The horses never stayed on the bus, though. They really did a quick walk through.

This wasn't the first time one of Williams' horses has boarded a Detroit-area bus. He told WXYZ 7 that he intended for the stunt to make a splash, as he's had horses "on Jefferson, we've been on the Chalmers, we've been on the Connors and now on the 7 Mile." This was Raven's first bus adventure, though. Raven is a 12-year-old horse, and one of Williams' newest. Along with his 11 other horses, he watches 10 horses for individuals on his 10-acre property in Romulus, along with the typical barnyard set up of chickens, goats, pigs, a cow, barn cats, dogs, a parrot, snake, and others.

DDOT issued a statement to WXYZ November 10 that noted it is "taking the appropriate steps to address this incident as it is not consistent with DDOT policy and potentially creates an unsafe and uncomfortable ride for our passengers." The rider in the video seemed to be the only person on the bus at the time, and appeared pretty chill about the whole experience while he took some pictures. Also, it could be argued that the horses didn't technically "ride" the bus. It never moved while they were on board.

The city is using the recent attention as a way to train everyone at DDOT to "make sure they're aware of different policies," i.e. service animals. A statement from the city mentioned that they recognized "that the actions in the video were meant to draw awareness to a positive cause. The City of Detroit also stands ready to assist our local entrepreneurs by connecting them with programs and opportunities that safely increase awareness of their organizations, and helps them expand their positive impact on our City.".

Sources indicate that williams' act was truly wholesome, and of course people understand horses don't technically belong on a bus, or in a city environment with all those dangerous cars. Take it from last city to truly hold out on keeping horses around — Latest York City, which finally voted away its famous horse carriages in October.

#6452. The Chevy El Camino Launched In 1959, And This Is The Ute's Most Sought-After Model Year

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (578 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

The Chevy El Camino Launched In 1959, And This Is The Ute's Most Sought-After Model Year

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that no, the Chevy El Camino wasn't the first to combine a two-door car with an open bed truck.
  • According to recent reports, of course, it was the 1957 Ford Ranchero that truly inspired the El Camino.
  • Recent findings suggest that this is where things start to get interesting for gearheads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that no, the Chevy El Camino wasn't the first to combine a two-door car with an open bed truck. The first production vehicle to do that was a Ford, but possibly not the one you're thinking of. A design engineer named Lew Bandt, then with Ford of Australia, developed what's often considered the original factory-made ute — the 1934 Ford Model 40-A Light Delivery. Depending on exactly how you define a ute, some folks point to the 1927 Volvo OV4 as well.

According to recent reports, of course, it was the 1957 Ford Ranchero that truly inspired the El Camino. The Ranchero was built on the Blue Oval's full-size platform of the time, and it became both relatively popular and relatively profitable for the automaker. In fact, it was successful enough that Chevy was inspired to get in on the ute action with its full-size 1959 El Camino. Originally a short-lived model only in production for that year and 1960, the El Camino would get a second chance at life in 1964. That's when the Bowtie brand revived the name and brought it back in slightly downsized form on the same platform as the intermediate-class Chevrolet Chevelle.

Recent findings suggest that this is where things start to get interesting for gearheads. In 1970, Chevrolet introduced a 454-cubic-inch LS6 V8 that was reserved for both the Chevelle and its platform mate. With that mill standing out as the most powerful unit of the year, the former became a muscle-car legend and one of Dom Toretto's rides in the epic 10-movie "Fast and Furious" saga. Meanwhile, the latter turned into perhaps the most sought-after El Camino of them all, the 1970 El Camino SS LS6 454. Keep in mind that this was a whole different engine than the LS6 in the 200-mph 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray.

Sources indicate that there are two key reasons that enthusiasts crave this machine. Right off the bat, the 1970 El Camino SS 454 was a one-year wonder — its exact powerplant was the aggressive LS6 V8 that would be dropped from the El Camino for 1971. True, Chevy sold a 1971 El Camino SS 454, but that mill was the less-powerful LS5. As far as actual production numbers for the 1970 model, those are hard to come by. Hemmings says 4,475 Chevrolets in total were sold with the LS6 for that year, but they were spread out among both Chevelles and El Caminos.

Sources indicate that the second major selling point here is the outrageous driving experience offered by these rides, and for that, credit also goes to their incredible engine. Factory rated at 450 horsepower with a whopping 500 pound-feet of torque, this motor featured a cast-iron block and heads along with an 11.25:1 compression ratio. Also adding to the muscle are a four-bolt main block, a four-barrel Holley carburetor, and a high-performance camshaft. The outcome was that both the El Camino and Chevelle could serve up more horses than not just the 1970 Corvette, but all other production cars, too.

In a recent development, as further proof of just how hard people are jonesing for the 1970 El Camino SS LS6 454, an example may hold the record for the highest auction price for any El Camino — the car went for $275,000 at a Barrett-Jackson sale in 2023. Just remember auction values can change promptly: one 1970 Chevelle LS6 lost its owner a million dollars.

#6451. Rocket Fuel: The Last Frontier For Natural Gas

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1563 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Rocket Fuel: The Last Frontier For Natural Gas

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1563 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fossil fuels are slowly beginning to lose their grip on the global transportation sector, with one key omission: rocket fuel.
  • Not all rocket fuel is methane-based, but that’s where some aerospace firms, including SpaceX, have landed in the pursuit of space domination.
  • With its future volume of launch operations in mind, SpaceX aims to exercise as much control as possible over its fuel supply.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fossil fuels are slowly beginning to lose their grip on the global transportation sector, with one key omission: rocket fuel. The rocket fuel conundrum has earned an uptick in attention in recent years, now that rocket launches, once rare, are becoming as commonplace as rush hour traffic. The Elon Musk venture SpaceX, for example, is building fresh natural gas pipelines in order to produce its own methane-based propellant, needed to sustain the launch of many thousands of rockets in the coming years.

Not all rocket fuel is methane-based, but that’s where some aerospace firms, including SpaceX, have landed in the pursuit of space domination. Methane is processed from natural gas, stripping away nitrogen and other impurities. Liquefied and mixed with liquid oxygen, it becomes a powerful propellant.

With its future volume of launch operations in mind, SpaceX aims to exercise as much control as possible over its fuel supply. The company is investing in its own natural gas pipelines and on-site fuel production facilities to help ensure that the taps don’t run dry, though it still relies on the gas industry to find the stuff and bring it up from the ground.

SpaceX has already been sucking up a copious amount of natural gas for its existing operations in Texas and Florida. “SpaceX (SPCX) is emerging as one of the largest new customers for natural gas,” reported the oil and gas analytics firm East Daley in October.

“Unlike Falcon 9, which burns rocket-grade kerosene and liquid oxygen, Starship creates a direct link between launch activity and natural gas consumption. SPCX plans to process and liquefy pipeline gas into liquid methane to fuel the rockets,” East Daley elaborates.

As described by East Daley, the SpaceX subsidiary Coastal Connect Services is planning a 32.4-mile natural gas pipeline to hook up SpaceX operations in Cape Canaveral, Florida with existing infrastructure jointly owned by Kinder Morgan and Energy Transfer.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, at the company’s launch site and newly incorporated (as of 2025) City of Starbase in Cameron County, Texas, looks are in motion for SpaceX affiliate Lone Star Mineral Development to connect the newly introduced 8-mile “Starpipe” natural gas pipeline with another 145-mile pipeline right now being built by the firms WhiteWater, Enbridge, and MPLX. Starpipe is expected to begin shuttling natural gas into Starbase Texas early next year.

Industry observers note that the two pipeline projects come alongside word that SpaceX has nailed down approvals for parts of a new $100 billion project that expands the firm’s US footprint into another combination city-and-launch-site under the name of Starbase, Louisiana. The new city will presumably also require a reliable supply of natural gas for on-site rocket fuel production.

For the record, Starbase, Louisiana is not part of the educational non-profit organization STARBASE Louisiana, an affiliate of the national STARBASE program of the US Department of Defense, aimed at stimulating interest in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) topics among 5th grade students. The Louisiana branch of STARBASE is located Barksdale Air Force Base in Bossier Parish, in the northwestern part of the state.

Sources indicate that starbase, Louisiana will take up 125,000 acres of land at Pecan Island in a marshy region along the southern coast in Vermilion Parish, where plans are being laid for 30 introduces per day. More than a dozen launch towers will eventually sprout up at the site, where the operation will include producing rocket fuel.

If you’ve gotten wind of the project under the name “Osprey,” you’re not dreaming. The new city was reportedly code-named “Project Osprey” during initial discussions with public officials. As described by the Gulf State News affiliate WWNO (New Orleans Public Radio) on November 11, Project Osprey was shrouded in secrecy during the initial negotionas, with “dozens” of local officials signing non-disclosure agreements that limited what they could say about the project.

Industry observers note that the Osprey code name also reportedly enabled Vermilion Parish officials to sidestep public participation in ostensibly public hearings on the Starbase, Louisiana project earlier this year. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry finally let the cat out of the bag in a public announcement in August. Local residents and the nonprofit organization Vermillion Citizens coalition have already filed a lawsuit against the project, alleging that parish officials approved parts of Starbase, Louisiana in violation of the state’s Open Public Meetings Law.

If and when shovels hit the ground on Starbase, Louisiana, the Trump administration is taking steps to help ensure that natural gas producers in the US come through with the goods — not just for SpaceX, of course, although the firm has become a market-mover in the gas industry as noted by East Daley.

In a recent development, on November 10, for example, the US Department of Energy confirmed the finishing touches on a $480 million loan in support of Project Elkhorn, an endeavor under the umbrella of the oil and gas firm Arena Energy. Project Elkhorn covers the modernization of 22 existing platforms off the Louisiana coast — coincidentally or not, the same state that expects to host the new Starbase city.

Industry observers note that arena launched in 1999 with a focus on revitalizing mature oil and gas fields. According to the Energy Department, Project Elkhorn will ramp natural gas production up to 77 million cubic feet per day at peak production among the 22 platforms, alongside up to 38,600 barrels of oil per day. By way of contrast, the 22 platforms at the moment produce 30,000 barrels of oil per day. Over the lifespan of Project Elkhorn, the collective total is expected to add 25 million barrels of oil and 250 billion cubic feet of natural gas to the US fossil energy roster.

As CEO of the leading EV maker Tesla, Elon Musk has earned his share of credit for rescuing electric cars from the dustbin of automotive obscurity and vaulting them into the mainstream mobility market of today — if not so much here in the US, then certainly overseas. Musk’s other ventures, on the other hand, threaten to offset, if not override, whatever sustainability gains are to be made from EVs.

In addition to SpaceX, Musk’s xAI data centers have also contributed to spiking demand for natural gas. Last year word dropped that Musk’s Colossus data center in Memphis, Tennessee trucked in approximately three dozen industrial-sized gas generators to power the site, at least 15 of which were already in operation without an air quality permit. The Southern Environmental Law Center has been among those raising the alarm over toxic emissions from the generators, which lack the pollution controls required of permanent power plants.

It has been revealed that natural gas also factors into a fresh data center planned for the SpaceX-backed City of Starbase, Texas, which sits adjacent to Brownsville. The city of Brownsville recently imposed a temporary moratorium on new data center construction. According to ABC News affiliate KVUE and other sources, earlier this year Elon Musk asked Brownsville officials to de-annex a parcel of land at its outskirts, evidently in order to building a $24 billion data center at the site along with a new gas-fired power plant for a new data center to be located in Starbase. The request was granted, enabling the project to skirt around the Brownsville moratorium.

Starbase city officials are scheduled to conduct a public hearing on the upcoming data center on December 9, where presumably they will decide whether or not the project can make due with gas generators until a full gas power plant with appropriate pollution controls can materialize.

Over and above the rocket fuel glitch, grassroots activists, environmental organizations, and researchers have been raising the alarm over the impact of Starbase in Texas for years, tracking significant harm to local public recreation resources as well as wildlife habitats. Similar concerns have surfaced around SpaceX’s looks for Starbase, Louisiana.

Recent findings suggest that of course, nobody seriously expects the whole domestic rocket business to stop in its tracks. The issue is one of mitigating climate and biodiversity risks, developing projects that avoid pummeling vulnerable communities with additional public health risks, and investing in more sustainable options including alternative rocket fuels.

Keep an eye on the aviation industry for some hints at the future of sustainable propellants. Airline stakeholders have been focusing on SAF, generally meaning a bio-based equivalent of kerosene jet fuel. However, the going has been slow, and it’s even slower in the field of propellants. The European Space Agency, for example, has been exploring green propellants for space operations for 25 years, with little to show for its efforts.

More recently, though, aviation stakeholders have begun turning to the emerging electrofuels or “solar fuels” industry, meaning fuels synthesized from captured carbon and green hydrogen, with solar and other renewables powering the operation. The green hydrogen industry has been struggling for traction, but signs of scaleup have finally emerged, with e-kerosene jet fuel in play along with green hydrogen. Honda, for one, is envisioning a fleet of reusable rockets propelled by renewable fuels, and at least two Chinese firms are also working the reusable rocket angle.

#6450. This 40-Year-Old Econobox Has The Top EPA MPG Rating Of Any Non-Hybrid Production Car

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (753 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

This 40-Year-Old Econobox Has The Top EPA MPG Rating Of Any Non-Hybrid Production Car

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Welp, we may have finally reached a turning point.
  • Now, we'll get into some of the details about the Sprint ER below, but first let's head off some possible objections at the pass.
  • Recent findings suggest that some drivers have also topped 60 mpg in real-world diesel driving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welp, we may have finally reached a turning point. Yes, short-sighted automakers have been supporting Trump's move to roll back fuel-economy standards. But voters seemed to have had other ideas on Election Day 2026, when the Dems secured both the Senate and House. Of course, while that may stop some of the madness, we're unlikely to see another fuel-sipper like the 1986 Chevrolet Sprint ER anytime soon. Chevy's tiny captive import originally posted an EPA highway rating of 60 mpg, a mark that no other non-electrified production car in the country has matched since. Plus, that highway score was complemented by ratings of 55 mpg in the city and 57 mpg combined.

Now, we'll get into some of the details about the Sprint ER below, but first let's head off some possible objections at the pass. The most important is that the EPA made a major change in how it calculates fuel efficiency back in 2007 and then retroactively updated its database. As a result, the 1986 Sprint ER presently demonstrates an EPA line of 44 mpg city/53 mpg highway/48 mpg combined. That makes for decreases of approximately 20%/12%/16% compared to its original fuel-economy grades.

Recent findings suggest that some drivers have also topped 60 mpg in real-world diesel driving. A writer for Car and Driver, for example, hypermiled a 2017 Chevy Cruze diesel to the tune of 70 mpg over a test run of about 160 miles. It's just that diesel engines have some drawbacks of their own.

Industry observers note that in a way, the genesis of the Chevy Sprint goes back to some of America's earlier meddling in the Middle East. The CIA had put Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi in control of Iran in 1953 — forcing out that country's democratically elected prime minister — and the shah was then overthrown himself as part of the 1979 Iranian Revolution. That led to the oil crisis of the same year, which helped convince GM to enter a three-way partnership with Isuzu and Suzuki in 1981. The goal was to build high-efficiency cars that were, basically, too small for GM to build at the time.

One of those cars was the JDM Suzuki Cultus, a car that would be renamed the Swift in Europe in 1985 and be rebadged as the Chevrolet Sprint for the same year. It also served as the Pontiac Firefly, but only in Canada. Now, this wasn't as tiny as a kei car, but it certainly wasn't massive. That 1986 Sprint checked in at 144 inches long, 60 inches wide, and 53 inches tall — so it was about 1 inch longer than the 2022 Chevy Spark, but also 2.8 inches narrower, 5.4 inches shorter in height, and 774 pounds lighter. After all, the Sprint ER, a three-door hatchback, tipped the scales at only 1,504 pounds.

Yet svelte dimensions weren't the only factors in play. The regular Sprint was motivated by a 1.0-liter I3 engine capable of 48 horsepower, and Suzuki had revised the camshaft for the ER version. It made a significant difference, since the non-ER model had an original EPA line of 44/50/47 (37/45/40 in today's ratings).

For this section, please keep in mind we're going to level the playing field by using the post-2008 EPA ratings for the Sprint ER — which, as a reminder, features a fuel-economy line of 44/53/48 with its standard five-speed manual gearbox. Nowadays, the most fuel-efficient non-electrified car in the country is the 2026 Honda Civic that can see 32/41/36 with its 2.0-liter I4 motor and CVT. The 2026 Civic Hybrid, as an FYI, can raise the efficiency bar to 50/47/49.

Recent findings suggest that the latter model isn't the country's most efficient hybrid, either. For that, we have to turn to the Toyota Prius. Sure, it gets an electric boost from its hybrid setup, yet the Prius may be the next gas-powered car to reach the 60 mpg club. The latest EPA line, for the 2027 Prius, is 59/50/55. Oddly, the 2026 Prius is listed at 57/56/57, and Toyota hasn't revealed what's changed. The same year Prius further led the way among hybrids with the best real-world gas mileage, at least according to Consumer Reports.

And the most efficient EVs can routinely see triple-digit MPGe figures with the EPA. The Lucid Air Pure, with rear-wheel drive and 19-inch wheels, sets the pace in this regard. It can squeeze out 149 MPGe in the city, complemented by grades of 142 MPGe highway and 146 MPGe combined.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The uninformed often fall for the illusion that high-speed rail is simply a railroad operating extremely fast trains.
  • In a recent development, the FRA defines three tiers of Passenger Equipment Safety Standards delineated by top speed.
  • The agency stipulates that high-speed trains can't travel faster than 160 mph on any track with at-grade crossings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The uninformed often fall for the illusion that high-speed rail is simply a railroad operating extremely fast trains. In actuality, it's an entire transportation system tightly regulated by government agencies. The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) attempted to spur high-speed rail development in 2018 by letting operators run high-speed trains on existing speed-limited infrastructure, but so far, no fresh service has usurped Amtrak's Acela on the Northeast Corridor as America's fastest train. Businesses simply won't buy passenger trains capable of hitting 220 miles per hour if they don't have the dedicated right-of-way needed to reach top speed.

In a recent development, the FRA defines three tiers of Passenger Equipment Safety Standards delineated by top speed. Each increasing tier requires more stringent crashworthiness, maintenance, and safety standards. Most passenger trains in the United States fall under Tier I, which is limited to 125 mph. Tier II, or higher-speed rail, has a legal top speed of 160 mph. Tier III, established in 2018, allows for speeds up to 220 mph. However, the trains are only half of the equation.

The agency stipulates that high-speed trains can't travel faster than 160 mph on any track with at-grade crossings. Even tracks with a 160 mph limit are rare in the U.S., as the Northeast Corridor has only four short stretches where Acela trains are allowed to touch 160 mph. The rest of the route between Boston and Washington, D.C. is limited to 125 mph. With as many as 386 passengers on board, there can't be any risk of anyone or anything entering the tracks and causing a catastrophic crash.

Japan's Shinkansen is viewed as the archetypal form of high-speed rail. The moniker translates into English as "new main line." Japanese National Railways opened the first Shinkansen line between Tokyo and Osaka in 1964. The five-year construction effort created a new dedicated high-speed main line, separate from commuter and freight traffic on the parallel Tōkaidō Main Line. France's TGV and other high-speed networks in Europe borrowed this dedicated-infrastructure philosophy from the Shinkansen.

Florida's Brightline is the most prominent U.S. example of the failings of shared rights-of-way. The higher-speed service between Miami and Orlando is heavily constrained by its 325-mile route, specifically the portion shared with the Florida East Coast Railway. According to Brightline, its trains are limited to 79 mph along this section. The 67-mile stretch between Miami and West Palm Beach, owned by the freight service, has 156 at-grade crossings. The abundance of crossings creates opportunities for trains to hit vehicles and pedestrians. Brightline-involved collisions have killed over 200 people since 2017. Dedicated rights-of-way are not only faster, they are far safer.

How to Lose Weight Naturally, According to Experts

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in.
  • Industry observers note that starting a weight-loss journey is no easy feat.
  • According to recent reports, but at its core, weight loss is about developing a healthy, sustainable relationship with food and movement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Industry observers note that starting a weight-loss journey is no easy feat. There’s a lot to think about, between getting into a regular workout routine, changing up what you eat, and maybe even considering a GLP-1 medication.

According to recent reports, but at its core, weight loss is about developing a healthy, sustainable relationship with food and movement. You don’t have to make a dozen changes all at once—the goal is long-term success, even if it’s a slow process. That’s why you should aim to lose one to two pounds a week, states Danielle Crumble Smith, RDN, a dietitian at Eat Well, Live Well. Working out at a manageable pace, eating balanced meals, and making maintainable changes can help you feel your best.

Industry observers note that meet the experts: Danielle Crumble Smith, RDN, is a nutritionist at Eat Well, Live Well. Kami Blease, CPT, is a personal trainer at Fyt Personal Training. Tatyana Johnston, CPT, is a former Nike master trainer and event specialist at Lululemon. Jordan Hill, RD, is a nutritionist with Top Nutrition Coaching.

Ahead, experts share their 10 best tips to make your weight-loss journey successful.

First, be sure to consult your doctor—they’ll help you set mindful, attainable goals that will keep your body healthy and strong. Then, try implementing more of these habits into your lifestyle:.

According to recent reports, take the stairs every day at work or hold a quick plank first thing in the morning. "All these things add up over time," claims Kami Blease, CPT, a personal trainer at Fyt Personal Training. "I recommend finding things you could do almost daily.”.

Sources indicate that additionally, try adding a brisk 30-minute walk into your day (even if it’s broken up into three 10-minute walks) to increase calorie burn and push you closer to your weight-loss goals, per the Mayo Clinic. "It's low impact and not a super strenuous form of movement, which increases the chances that someone will stick with it,” states Tatyana Johnston, CPT, a former Nike master trainer and event specialist at Lululemon. "Just remember to recover with hydration, fuel, and stretching.”.

Burn fat and build muscle with the WH+ 4-week walking proposal.

Strength training “helps with balance and stability, improves metabolism, and even lowers your risk of certain diseases," states Blease. Resistance training has also been found to help with weight loss and body recomposition, according to a 2026 study in Frontiers in Endocrinology that had 304 adults follow a calorie-restricted diet and either resistance train, do aerobic exercise, or no exercise for 1 to 18 months.

Sources indicate that to get comfortable with form, try practicing bodyweight exercises first, Blease recommends, then add weights after you’ve mastered the move. This can help you focus on progressive overload—which means gradually increasing the weight, frequency, or number of reps over time, Blease indicates. Eventually, you should aim to work all major muscle groups at least twice a week, per the fresh ACSM resistance training guidelines.

In a recent development, cardio can also help with weight loss—the CDC recommends 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity (such as brisk walking) per week, or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity activity (like running) each week. However, this number can vary based on someone’s individual health, and the intensity of the cardio. "Consistency is key. If you can establish and stick to a cardio schedule, you have a better chance at losing weight and keeping it off," Johnston indicates. Playing sports, working out with friends, or listening to a podcast during cardio can help boost your motivation too.

Industry observers note that also, if you enjoy high-impact exercises and want to lose weight fast, HIIT workouts can be a great way to expend a lot of energy in a short period of time. "You can ramp up the intensity by trying to get in more reps during a certain amount of time or using heavier weights while maintaining the same time goal,” notes Blease. “Both will increase your intensity and continue to challenge your body.".

Lululemon Ebb to Street Tank Top.

Alo Airlift High-Waist Suit Up Legging.

It has been revealed that if the gym or workout classes aren’t really your speed, choose a form of movement that you love so you can stay consistent with it. “Hiking, swimming, skiing, surfing, or biking are all forms of movement that might feel more sustainable,” says Blease.

Industry observers note that "Start smaller than you might think," Blease says. "Often, people overcommit because they are excited. However, it's then easy to get burnt out." After a few weeks, add in a second day, and when that feels seamless, try a third, and over time, you'll find a cadence that works for you, she adds.

In a recent development, just make sure you always have at least one rest day. "People can get so fixated on weight loss that they end up [overdoing exercise and] hurting themselves," Blease claims. "Take time to stretch, rest, and recover as needed.".

"Having a trainer create a program that is specific to your needs ensures that you are more likely to get the results you are looking for—and keep your body safe in the process," says Blease. They can help you lose fat while building muscle, which can better your overall metabolic health and insulin sensitivity, and regulate blood sugar to support a healthier body recomposition.

A trainer will also make sure you maintain proper form and that you stay consistent. Decide on a number of days per week that fits your goal and budget, and ask your trainer to help hold you accountable, Blease claims.

Industry observers note that research suggests that working with a personal trainer may have more profound effects on weight loss: A 2024 study in Heliyon had 66 adults train individually, with a partner, or a personal trainer over 12 weeks, and they monitored their improvements in bench presses, squats, skeletal muscle mass, and fat mass. The group that worked with a personal trainer improved their leg training and reduced fat mass compared to the other groups.

It has been revealed that protein can help you stay full throughout the day, stabilize your blood sugar levels, and synthesize muscle mass, Smith says, helping with weight loss. While individual dietary needs vary, you can generally aim for 30 to 35 grams of protein per meal to help you stay full throughout the day. Some good sources include eggs, poultry, seafood, red meat, beans, peas, lentils, legumes, nuts, seeds, and soy, per the current Dietary Guidelines for Americans.

Sources indicate that additionally, "fiber is more slowly digested and helps keep you feeling full for a longer period,” Smith adds, recommending vegetables. Increased vegetable intake is also linked to lower blood sugar levels, lower triglycerides, and can help promote liver function. If you don't love veggies, you can also puree them and add them to a sauce or weight-loss-friendly smoothie.

According to recent reports, lastly, don’t forget about healthy (unsaturated) fats—which can help provide energy, per the Mayo Clinic. Try avocados, extra-virgin olive oil, nuts, seeds, soybeans, and seafood.

"Drinking enough water can help you to feel full and prevent overeating," claims dietitian Jordan Hill, RD. Aim to drink about half your body weight in ounces of hydrating fluids per day.

It has been revealed that also, avoid sugary beverages. "Juices, sodas, and fancy coffees are often the calorie-equivalent of a meal, yet they will still leave you hungry," says Smith. "The sugar content is often more than a candy bar, which will cause blood sugar levels to rise." Instead, replace your beverages with fruit-infused water, herbal tea, or coffee with cinnamon or zero-calorie sweeteners.

Avoid foods that are high in added sugars, unhealthy fats, and empty calories, which can contribute to weight gain, says Hill: "Instead, focus on eating whole, nutrient-dense foods that will provide your body with the nutrients it needs.".

In a recent development, listening to your internal cues of hunger and fullness can help you control portion sizes, which can also aid weight loss. "Honoring fullness can help prevent overeating and ensure that you're not consuming more calories than your body needs," states Hill. Keeping a food journal can also help you become more mindful of what you're eating, when, and how you're feeling throughout the process of losing weight.

“When you skip meals or go too long in between meals or snacks, you get overly hungry. This makes it much more difficult to make healthy choices, and it also makes it harder to not overeat later," notes Smith. Skipping meals can also result in a slower metabolism and leave you feeling fatigued, which can negatively impact your workouts both in effort and recovery.

If you struggle to eat consistent meals, Smith recommends munching on small snacks throughout the day. “Set yourself up for success by bringing healthy snacks with you when you’re away from home, so you’re not caught in a situation where you are really hungry but have no access to healthy food,” she indicates.

It has been revealed that if you need extra assistance, a dietitian can analyze your diet and recommend personalized tips for how you can eat to lose weight, which may be more helpful than doing it on your own. A 2025 review of articles on weight-loss interventions provided by a dietitian for overweight and obese adults in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics looked at how working with a dietitian improved their health markers, as opposed to not working with one (the control group). The group that worked with a dietitian had improved weight loss, waist circumference, blood pressure, and quality of life compared to the control group.

When you encounter a setback (like when you skip a few days of workouts), it can be discouraging and all-consuming, and can cause you to fall off track. "One of the most crucial components of successfully reaching a goal is to not let setbacks ruin our progress,” claims Johnston. “The setback is often not as severe as we think, and will not impact our end goal very much at all.”.

Just take a breath and realize we’re all human and mistakes are normal; then move forward with your health proposal in mind.

And don’t forget to be kind to yourself. Practicing self-compassion and returning to your proposal will help reinforce your goal and remind you that this weight-loss journey requires patience and perseverance. "Practice giving yourself grace when [you] slip up,” Johnston says. “As long as it doesn’t become a habit, you will continue moving forward towards your goal.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SOLRITE Unveils Next-Gen Virtual Power Plant Node with sonnen and ADAPT Energy, Integrating VPP Breakers to Turn Home Loads into Flexible Grid Assets.

ADAPT Energy’s control of VPP breakers will add dispatchable load flexibility to the SOLRITE sonnen VPP, while paving a simpler, faster, and lower-cost path to whole-home backup.

According to recent reports, SOLRITE, a company specializing in developing, financing, and owning Virtual Power Plant Agreement (VPA) projects, together with Sonnen, a leader in Virtual Power Plant energy storage technology, revealed they will now digitally integrate VPP smart breakers, managed by ADAPT Energy, into the SOLRITE  sonnen VPP. The integration marks the next evolution of sonnen and SOLRITE’s industry-leading partnership in VPP innovation, expanding beyond battery storage by transforming residential electrical loads into flexible, dispatchable grid assets for both the VPP and smart backup power applications.

Industry observers note that unlike traditional approaches to whole-home backup, often requiring hard-wired circuit relocation, including exclusive loads panels, the newly expanded VPP Node combines the sonnenHub with ADAPT Energy’s VPP smart breaker technology to intelligently manage major household loads. This creates a more streamlined approach to whole-home backup while unlocking an entirely newly introduced source of flexibility for the SOLRITE sonnen VPP. With homeowner permission, the VPP smart breaker—controlled by ADAPT Energy—can also participate in on-grid VPP events, enabling the same electrical infrastructure to be flexible for both backup and grid participation.

Recent findings suggest that “Our work with ADAPT Energy is a meaningful step forward in how we think about residential battery storage and VPP participation,” stated Regan George, CEO and Founder of SOLRITE Energy. “We have already demonstrated the tremendous value of connecting sonnen batteries together as a pooled grid asset. Now, we’re going inside the home and unlocking another layer of flexibility that has been sitting there all along. By combining the battery with additional load management made possible by the VPP smart breaker technology, we’re creating a more valuable node for the grid while also giving homeowners a clever backup solution.”.

Sources indicate that the integration addresses one of the longstanding challenges of whole-home backup: how to provide broad electrical coverage without having large household loads drain available battery capacity too rapidly or cause the nano-grid to immediately fail after an off-grid transition due to excessive inrush current. With the newly expanded VPP smart breaker technology digitally integrated with the sonnen ecosystem, the system can intelligently shed large loads without requiring those circuits to be relocated. ADAPT Energy keeps the smart breakers synchronized with the sonnen battery during backup mode and automatically restores the breakers when grid power returns. This significantly reduces installation complexity and tedious inspections for installers, allowing crews to complete more jobs per week.

It has been revealed that for homeowners, the system provides the convenience of a whole-home electrical configuration that intelligently manages the loads that have the greatest impact on backup duration. This work is all done in the background, meaning homeowners do not have to worry about resetting individual circuits during an outage. Instead, participating homes will see more value from their VPA program in the form of an enhanced backup power experience. Furthermore, at any time in the future, if a homeowner is interested in altering which of their VPP smart breaker-controlled loads are shed during an outage, the process to make such a change is quick and easy, requiring no electrical reconfiguration.

“This is about making whole-home backup work the way homeowners expect it to,” said Troy Morgan, President of PanTech Design, the developer of ADAPT Energy. “Instead of putting the pressure on homeowners to change the way their home is wired and to manually manipulate loads during an outage, we’re putting intelligence into their energy system, which provides a seamless and automatic backup power experience for their home. Our technology empowers home loads to supply optimal backup power during an outage or provide valuable flexibility to the grid.”.

The permission-based architecture aligns the interests of the homeowner, battery owner and utility. The real opportunity comes when homeowners choose to opt in to allow the breakers to participate in on-grid VPP events.

It has been revealed that when a VPP event is dispatched, the sonnen battery can discharge or charge in concert with direct load shedding via ADAPT. ADAPT Energy will strictly shed pre-approved household loads, and by using Eaton AbleEdge breakers, ADAPT achieves this right where the breaker sits, without relocation. A customer who has opted to include a pool pump, for example, can have that load temporarily turned off while the sonnen battery is discharging to the grid. That way, the VPP can respond through both energy stored in the battery and energy that would have otherwise been consumed by the home, thereby increasing the dispatched injection into the grid, by the VPP.

Industry observers note that “With the addition of ADAPT Energy’s VPP smart-breaker technology to the SOLRITE–sonnen ecosystem, we are expanding the virtual power plant from a battery-centered resource into a fully orchestrated home-energy platform,” remarked Blake Richetta, Chairman and CEO of sonnen Inc. “By synchronizing energy that has been harnessed in our battery with intelligent, real-time control of household electrical loads, we can deliver more flexible, responsive capacity to the grid precisely when it is needed most. This integration materially strengthens the value of SOLRITE’s virtual power plant—supporting grid reliability, creating greater customer value, and enabling SOLRITE to continue delivering industry-leading solar-plus-storage VPA solutions to homeowners.”.

Press release from www.sonnenusa.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taylor Swift has once again found herself at the center of the cultural conversation, as she's set to return to her country music roots and take the stage at the 2026 CMA Awards—her first performance at the event in 13 years.

Recent findings suggest that the pop star's last sang an acoustic rendition of her hit song "Red" at the awards show in 2013. While it's anyone's guess what Swift, 36, will do this year, she's among the nominees for Single of the Year, thanks to "I Knew It, I Knew You" from "Toy Story 5.".

The ceremony is also set to hold a special tribute for country music legend, Dolly Parton, who passed away at the age of 80 on Aug. 25. It's unclear if Swift will be part of the memorial.

Of course, the "Patient Zero" singer is no stranger to speculation, especially after the busy year she's had both professionally and personally. Over the summer, Swift tied the knot with Kansas City Chiefs tight end, Travis Kelce in a star-studded ceremony at Madison Square Garden.

The newlyweds also seemingly have their hands full with a newly introduced $5.35. million sprawling lakefront estate in Ohio, not far from Kelce's childhood home. But it's not the only impressive dwelling in the singer's headline-worthy real estate empire.

Over the years, the 14-time Grammy winner has assembled a multimillion-dollar property portfolio that includes eight homes.

The collection spans across New York, Rhode Island, Tennessee, California, Rhode Island, and Ohio, with each home reflecting a different chapter of her life and career.

The singer, who reached superstardom after the release of her 2006 self-titled debut album, has homebuying down to an art.

Let's take a look at some of the properties the Grammy winner has scooped up over the years—from a glamorous landmarked Beverly Hills abode to a downtown Manhattan compound, and more.

Swift grew up on a picturesque Christmas tree farm near Reading, PA, and she honored her childhood home in her 2019 song “Christmas Tree Farm.”.

Swift's father, Scott, purchased the 11-acre farm from a client and spent time tending to the grounds when not working his full-time job at Merrill Lynch, according to Refinery29.

A few years later, Swift moved with her family to a nearby house in Wyomissing, PA.

When the property hit the market in 2022, fans got a rare look inside the Georgian-style estate.

Standout features of the five-bedroom house include a sun-drenched breakfast nook, a glossy brick fireplace, and plenty of wainscoting.

It has been revealed that the stately residence was listed for $1,099,000 in February and sold for $800,000 in June—a 27% reduction. Is this potential proof that not everything Swift-related turns to gold?

The family moved out of Pennsylvania when Swift was a teen.

In 2003, the family relocated to Hendersonville, TN, so that Swift could pursue a music career. Here, her parents paid $790,000 for a 6,758-square-foot home that sits 30 minutes by car from downtown Nashville.

Sources indicate that the waterfront home with "fantastic views" of the Cumberland River features four bedrooms, five bathrooms, and well over an acre. The family still owns the property.

Swift purchased a $2 million luxury condo in Nashville's vibrant Music Row neighborhood for herself just four years after signing a record deal with Significant Machine Records.

The three-bedroom, 4.5-bathroom penthouse boasts over 3,500 square feet of living space.

According to reports, she also scooped up the smaller one-bedroom apartment below hers that same year for $387,000. She's still the owner of both units.

Swift added another Tennessee property to her real estate portfolio when she snagged a Greek Revival mansion in the gated Northumberland Estate neighborhood of Nashville.

Recent findings suggest that the singer purchased the four-bedroom, 4.5-bathroom mansion in 2011 for $2.5 million. The classic mansion from 1934, which sits on 5 acres, is now estimated to be at least double what she paid.

It has been revealed that the glamorous home features a striking curved staircase, vaulted beam ceilings, floor-to-ceiling windows, and marble fireplaces. Swift purchased the property for her parents.

Swift shook things up in 2012 when she headed West and picked up a $1,775,000 midcentury modern home in Los Angeles.

The four-bedroom abode featured floor-to-ceiling windows, a private courtyard, a lagoon-style pool, and a 1,000-bottle wine cellar.

She sold the property six years later for $2.65 million, clearing nearly a million in profit.

You might have missed this quick flip. In late 2012, Swift bought a seven-bedroom waterfront home in Hyannis Port, MA, for $4.1 million.

The singer sold the property just a few months later for $5.67 million.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re well-versed in Swift’s discography, you're likely familiar with her Watch Hill, RI, retreat. Dubbed “Holiday House,” the historic abode was purchased by Swift for $17.75 million in 2013.

In a recent development, built in 1930, the extravagant seaside estate once belonged to composer and socialite Rebekah Harkness, who was married to William Hale "Bill" Harkness, “heir to the Standard Oil name and money,” as Swift sings. (Bonus points if you can name the song.).

The mansion features eight bedrooms, a 36-foot-long parlor, and an octagon-shaped dining room.

In 2014, the “Love Story” songstress purchased not one—but two—penthouses in Fresh York City’s ritzy Tribeca neighborhood.

The transaction included a 5,869-square-foot apartment for $14.85 million and a neighboring three-bedroom unit for $5.1 million.

Swift combined the two spaces, creating a massive nine-bedroom, nine-bathroom mega-apartment with wood-beamed ceilings, a dramatic curved staircase, and oversized windows.

She purchased a third unit in the building a few years later for $9.75 million, increasing her Fresh York City home’s layout by over 3,500 square feet.

Swift added a second West Coast abode to her portfolio when she purchased a historic Beverly Hills mansion for $25 million in 2015.

The lovely landmarked estate was once the home of movie producer Samuel Goldwyn, co-founder of Goldwyn Pictures.

Nestled on 2 acres in a cul-de-sac, the nearly 100-year-old home features a championship tennis court, a pool house, and a rose garden.

Despite her dalliances with the West Coast, Swift couldn’t get enough of Tribeca.

In 2017, the musician purchased yet another Tribeca property: the townhome adjacent to her massive penthouse.

In a recent development, the 5,000-square-foot townhouse was transformed into her private penthouse entrance, adding 3,660 square feet to her sprawling city residence. She paid a whopping $18 million for the three-story pad.

Swift famously lived in a sweet Cornelia Street carriage house for part of 2016 and 2017 while her gigantic Tribeca compound underwent renovations.

She rented the circa-1800s four-bedroom, five-bathroom West Village home, complete with blond parquet floors and antique brickwork, for $36,000 a month.

Swift famously immortalized the address in her song "Cornelia Street." It went back up for rent after Swift's departure and is at the moment off-market.

According to recent reports, in 2018, Swift’s father purchased a St. Petersburg, FL, penthouse for $4 million.

Industry observers note that residents of the luxe high-rise have access to 24/7 security, a top-notch fitness center, two heated swimming pools, and a billiards room. Even with the enhanced security, the home was burglarized in 2020.

Although Kelce is the one who snapped up the property, the newlyweds have a gorgeous new place to call home: a palatial eight-bedroom, 8.5-bathroom property the athlete purchased for $5.35 million in March.

The historic residence was built in 1895, and spans an impressive 21,140 square feet. The home was initially listed for $6.99 million in 2024, before the asking price was reduced to $5.99 million the following May.

Kelce secured the estate at a further discount, $1.64 million below its original asking price.

The Bratenahl, OH abode is close to Cleveland Heights, where Kelce grew up alongside his older brother, Jason Kelce.

The couple have worked to make the home a more private retreat, moving to add an 8-foot privacy wall that challenges a verbal warning when potential trespassers get too close.

The proposal had some trouble gaining approval, with a local regulation stating that solid fences and walls—as well as fences with less than 75% openness—cannot exceed 30 inches in height.

However, it seems they've gained quite a bit of support form neighbors, with one speaking anonymously to Page Six to push back on previous reports that the proposal had angered residents.

"I think they're excited," the neighbor told the outlet. "I think it's great. I don't think people are angry.".
