💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 10, 2026 at 1:10 pmNovember 10, 2026 at 1:28 pm.
  • Seattle will expand its police surveillance camera network to three more neighborhoods, Mayor Katie Wilson said Tuesday, ending a pause she put in place in March over privacy and civil liberties concerns.
  • The move comes a day after NYU’s Policing Project released an independent audit of the Seattle Police Department’s Real Time Crime Center (RTCC), which Wilson commissioned during the pause.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 10, 2026 at 1:10 pmNovember 10, 2026 at 1:28 pm.

Seattle will expand its police surveillance camera network to three more neighborhoods, Mayor Katie Wilson said Tuesday, ending a pause she put in place in March over privacy and civil liberties concerns.

The move comes a day after NYU’s Policing Project released an independent audit of the Seattle Police Department’s Real Time Crime Center (RTCC), which Wilson commissioned during the pause. The audit found the city had built “an key foundation” for overseeing the system but that “significant policy gaps remain.” It made 19 recommendations.

Cameras in the Stadium District, installed before this summer’s FIFA World Cup, will be turned on immediately, according to the mayor’s office. Cameras around Garfield High School and in the Capitol Hill nightlife district still need to be bought and installed, which will take months. The City Council approved all three areas in 2025.

Industry observers note that wilson briefly turned on the 22 stadium-area cameras during the World Cup, citing “credible threats” reported by law enforcement, and said they would go off after the tournament. The audit noted that police streamed live feeds throughout the event, despite a department policy against monitoring cameras without an active call or case.

“After reviewing the evidence, the recommendations, and the safeguards available to us, I believe there is an notable and responsible role for the RTCC within Seattle’s public-safety system,” Wilson remarked in a statement.

Wilson said the city will adopt most of the audit’s recommendations. The police department will publish a public dashboard on how the crime center is used and tighten its rules on data retention, permissible uses and requests from outside agencies. A new advisory group will help write policies for privately owned cameras, protests and where future cameras go.

In a recent development, no Flock cameras in Seattle, ever. Latest protections against potential abuses drawn from an outside audit. A handful of cameras in new neighborhoods. Here's what the RTCC looks like from the inside. pic.twitter.com/QeYUg8ZkW3.

Recent findings suggest that the Real Time Crime Center, which launched in 2025, pulls live video from hundreds of cameras into a single command room at police headquarters. They include 303 police-owned cameras at 61 sites, 116 security cameras at police buildings, 96 city traffic cameras, and 23 cameras owned by three local businesses that share their feeds with police.

It has been revealed that analysts watch 911 calls as they come in and pull up nearby cameras to give officers details callers may have missed, such as what a suspect is wearing or which way they ran. They also comb through recorded footage to help detectives investigate past crimes. The system runs on Fusus, software from Axon, the Arizona-based maker of police body cameras and Tasers.

According to recent reports, police are barred from using facial recognition with the system. The software does include an AI tool that searches video for people, vehicles and other objects, but analysts told auditors they use it only as a last resort because it is unreliable. In one case, a search for a man in a gray top and gray pants returned an image of a pigeon.

Whether the system reduces crime remains an open question. The Seattle Police Department has stated officers and detectives are three times more likely to make an arrest with help from crime center analysts, and that the center assisted in 17 homicide cases in 2025, helping close 10. But the audit notes that the department counts any analyst action as “support,” such as checking a camera, even if it produced nothing useful.

Industry observers note that broader research on crime centers is thin, the audit found, and studies of surveillance cameras on their own show mixed results. A University of Pennsylvania evaluation of Seattle’s program, commissioned by the city’s inspector general, isn’t expected until late 2027.

According to recent reports, critics have warned that footage could end up with federal immigration agents or out-of-state prosecutors pursuing people who come to Washington for abortions or gender-affirming care. The audit found that state and city laws limit such sharing, but they can’t fully prevent it. Outside agencies could still get footage through public records requests or court orders served on the city or on Axon, which stores some of the police department’s video in its cloud.

In a recent development, tee Sannon, technology policy program director for the ACLU of Washington, said the group was “deeply disappointed” by the decision. With the audit having “reaffirmed significant gaps in privacy protections and accountability,” expanding the network “is a step in the wrong direction,” Sannon said. She added that the city should invest in proven alternatives such as community violence prevention programs.

“Used together, CCTV and RTCC supercharge law enforcement’s capabilities to monitor, track, and reconstruct people’s movements across the city,” Sannon mentioned. Protecting residents, she said, requires strict, enforceable limits on how the technology is used, how long data is kept and who it’s shared with, along with independent oversight.

Wilson remarked the expansion and the fresh safeguards go together. “We can gather evidence to hold those who commit violent acts accountable and protect our neighbors targeted by federal overreach,” she said.

Business groups praised the decision. Jon Scholes, president and CEO of the Downtown Seattle Association, noted the city “already has stringent privacy guardrails in place” and that, with police staffing “still lagging,” additional tools “are essential for solving crimes.” The Seattle Metro Chamber and Challenge Seattle, which have pushed the city to turn on the cameras, cited a poll they commissioned this year that found 75% of Seattle voters support using cameras to help active investigations.

Recent findings suggest that “Residents and businesses have sent a clear message: they want our officers to have the tools to keep them safe,” remarked former Gov. Chris Gregoire, CEO of Challenge Seattle.

City Councilmember Bob Kettle, who chairs the council’s public safety committee, said the committee will take up the audit’s recommendations, along with those from the city’s inspector general and auditor.

Recent findings suggest that the city also plans to lay groundwork for connecting cameras run by Seattle Center tenants and nearby businesses to the crime center, according to the mayor’s office, citing interest from those businesses after the Bite of Seattle shooting in July. The audit flagged private camera integration as a key area to watch: the police department has bought about 100 devices that let businesses stream video to the center but hasn’t decided who will get them.

Recent findings suggest that the advisory group, which will include members of the Community Police Commission, the Community Surveillance Working Group, police and other city staff, will meet over the next few months. Its recommendations will then go through the police department’s policy review process.

JPMorgan Bitcoin positioning makes an interesting contrast with the current market panic. Bitcoin has plunged below $70,000, wiping out leveraged bullish bets and dragging major altcoins lower. Meanwhile, Michael Saylor’s Strategy faces another institutional headache after MSCI confirmed its removal from major equity indexes.

Wall Street might be seeing something that the market is missing. JPMorgan’s latest holdings show institutional exposure was growing before the latest sell-off, even as Strategy faces mounting pressure.

Could this be smart money positioning for Bitcoin’s next recovery?

JPMorgan held 848,932 Strategy shares worth $131.3 million at the end of September. That’s a 36% increase from its 624,387 shares reported three months earlier.

Its exposure to BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF grew even further in dollar terms. The bank reported 11.4 million IBIT shares worth $540 million, compared with 10.4 million shares valued at $355.7 million in June.

The IBIT position increased by 9.6% in share count, while its reported market value jumped 52%. JPMorgan also reported smaller positions in other Bitcoin funds, including Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust and Bitwise’s Bitcoin ETF.

Together, the Strategy and IBIT positions were worth $671 million at September 30. That’s a sizeable institutional footprint across two different ways of gaining Bitcoin exposure.

According to recent reports, however, the timing makes this filing particularly interesting. These holdings paint JPMorgan’s third quarter, ending September 30. JPMorgan was building exposure before Bitcoin’s latest breakdown, leaving investors wondering if the bank still sees value in the correction.

There is another detail worth watching. JPMorgan also disclosed substantial put-option exposure against Strategy and IBIT, alongside call positions. Its derivatives book shows a more complicated positioning strategy than a straightforward bullish bet. Still, the increased share counts show that the bank expanded its underlying holdings.

Tech Report: Seattle VC firm Ascend closes $17M fund to back ‘Third Act’ startups in physical AI and hardware

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1248 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 11, 2026 at 7:15 amNovember 11, 2026 at 7:30 am.
  • Venture firm Ascend has closed a $17 million third fund and landed its first institutional investor, in what founder Kirby Winfield calls the toughest fundraising market for small venture firms in 15 years.
  • According to recent reports, the Seattle-based firm invests at the earliest stage, often writing the first check into a startup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 11, 2026 at 7:15 amNovember 11, 2026 at 7:30 am.

Venture firm Ascend has closed a $17 million third fund and landed its first institutional investor, in what founder Kirby Winfield calls the toughest fundraising market for small venture firms in 15 years.

According to recent reports, the Seattle-based firm invests at the earliest stage, often writing the first check into a startup. It was the first investor in Overland AI, the maker of autonomous military vehicles, and an early backer of subsea geothermal startup Endurance Energy, among others.

Ascend Fund III will back more physical AI startups building robots, energy systems, defense technology and other ventures that blend software and hardware — part of a larger bet on what the Ascend team likes to call Seattle’s “Third Act.”.

In a recent development, winfield stated raising a third fund in this market reveals that Ascend has “arrived on the national stage,” along with Seattle’s rise as a hub for this upcoming class of startups. He said the firm’s track record puts it in the same league as the country’s top seed investors.

“We are not just some nice guys in the corner of the country helping out our neighbors,” said Winfield, who works closely with Jen Haller, Ascend partner and chief of staff, and Nate Bek, a principal at the firm.

Who’s backing the fund: The upcoming institutional investor is FirstLook Partners, a firm that invests in smaller venture funds. Josh Porter, FirstLook’s co-founder and managing partner, said the firm, which is “very bullish on the Seattle ecosystem,” looked at several startup markets outside San Francisco and New York and met many investors in Seattle, “but all roads kept leading back to Kirby.”.

Porter stated Winfield has “lived the founder journey” and has “the operational chops to sit across the table from a founder and empathize with what they’re going through.”.

The rest of the fund comes from family offices, founders who have sold companies, and more than a dozen founders of Ascend portfolio companies.

In a recent development, A tough market for small funds: Ascend’s raise comes as smaller venture firms struggle to bring in new money. Their investors, mostly wealthy individuals and family offices, are waiting longer for returns from earlier funds.

According to recent reports, just 211 newer venture firms closed at least one fund through the end of September, down from 927 in all of 2022, according to the PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor. Established firms took a record 88.2% of the money raised by U.S. venture funds in the first nine months of the year, the report found. Porter said smaller firms have to show “a right to exist and a right to win deals.”.

Recent findings suggest that ascend introduced its first fund in 2019 and ultimately raised $15 million. Its second fund closed at $25 million in 2023. The firm generally operates in the $15 million to $25 million range and writes the same size checks regardless of fund size, Winfield said.

“We think Kirby knows his place in the larger ecosystem, knows the value he brings to the table, and has sized his fund accordingly,” Porter said.

The firm has already drawn about 60% of the money committed to Fund III. GeekWire first reported that the firm was raising the fund in April 2025, based on filings at the time. Endurance was one of the firm’s first investments from the latest fund, in mid-2025.

In a recent development, ascend’s track record: Winfield started Ascend after two decades in leadership roles at four startups. He described the first fund as a proof of concept that “stumbled into some unicorns,” including Fabric, an e-commerce software company that was valued at $1.5 billion in 2022. Ascend was in its first round.

Sources indicate that with its second fund, Ascend moved away from consumer and marketplace investing to focus on enterprise AI and deep tech. Its most successful investments from that fund, according to Winfield, include Overland AI, Sabi, Yoodli and Zocks.

After Ascend’s first checks, its portfolio companies have gone on to raise more than $1.5 billion from investors including Accel, Benchmark, Bessemer, Founders Fund, Khosla and Lightspeed, according to Ascend.

It has been revealed that ascend’s second and third funds rank in the top 10% of funds of $50 million or less, based on current valuations of their portfolio companies, Winfield stated, citing figures Ascend shared with its investors at its annual meeting. The firm didn’t disclose specific returns or how much cash it has returned to its investors.

Sources indicate that what Ascend looks for: The firm looks for ideas that seem too difficult, too boring, too confusing or too small for significant multistage venture firms to evaluate. Ideally, Winfield said, its founders are doing something that makes Series A investors “a little bit nervous.”.

That’s why Ascend hasn’t made many more defense tech investments since backing Overland, he said. Valuations for well-known founders in the sector have soared as more investors have piled in.

“The time to invest in defense tech was when nobody was investing in defense tech,” Winfield said.

Porter said Ascend’s focus on Seattle and physical AI is “really the bet we made with Ascend,” adding that Endurance and Overland have the potential to become “generational, category-defining companies.”.

Fund III also backs AI software and infrastructure companies, including Seattle-area startup Govstream.ai, which uses AI to speed city permitting.

Seattle’s economic climate: Winfield is a champion of Seattle’s startup scene, known for Ascend’s annual Founders Bash party in the city and his ever-present ☔🔥☔ emojis on social media, symbolizing hot startups in rainy Seattle.

Ascend’s refreshed website and brand, released with Fund III, nod to the firm’s Seattle roots with its longstanding Seattle Startup Toolkit and a Spotify playlist of Pacific Northwest indie rock and hip-hop.

But Winfield has also been a vocal critic of state and local policies he sees as hostile to startups, including Washington’s new tax on income over $1 million, which takes effect in 2028 and survived a repeal vote last week. He worries the tax could eventually be extended to people earning $150,000 a year, which would make it harder for startups to recruit employees from places like Texas.

“The chilling effect that’s going to have on the ecosystem is real, and it’s happening,” he mentioned.

About 60% of Ascend’s portfolio companies are based in Seattle, according to the firm.

Bek said hardware companies such as Endurance and Overland still have good reasons to be in Seattle, including testing on Lake Union and in Yakima, access to the sea and University of Washington talent. For Overland, he said, that also means proximity to Joint Base Lewis-McChord.

Combined with the region’s history in aerospace, defense and energy, Winfield noted, those advantages make Seattle one of the country’s key hubs for building physical products. He called it “El Segundo Northwest,” a reference to the Los Angeles-area city that has become a hub for defense and hardware startups.

Industry observers note that as Winfield notes, Ascend isn’t the only early-stage firm chasing these companies. Pre-seed firms such as Cantos, Ironspring and Silent Ventures are backing similar founders, and some Seattle firms that historically focused on software are becoming more open to investing in hardware.

Ultimately, he remarked, Seattle still benefits from a long legacy of technical founders, and Ascend is “betting that those folks are going to continue to create companies that are worth hundreds of billions of dollars.”.

The trade group representing homeowners associations is calling for stronger protections after a shooting in Washington, DC, left a community manager dead.

The Community Association Institute remarked that it would renew efforts support laws that address harassment, threats, and intimidation against community managers before they escalate into violence.

Industry observers note that the group had pressed for such legislation in Nevada in 2025 and plans to do so at the federal level in 2027. New Jersey and Minnesota are also reportedly considering some legislation to address harassment.

Recent findings suggest that thursday's shooting in DC's Logan Circle neighborhood claimed the life of James “Jimmy” Stuart, manager of the Metropole and injured five others. The suspected shooter, Dr. Matt Wade Lambert, a resident of the complex, reportedly was in a dispute with the community over renovations he remarked damaged his penthouse unit.

“We mourn Jimmy's loss and extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and the entire Metropole community,” the CAI statement reads. “Our thoughts are also with the other victims, residents, and building staff whose lives have been forever changed by this tragedy.”.

Lambert was in the middle of a protracted legal dispute with his building's HOA at the time that the shooting happened.

Sources indicate that social median posts reputedly made by him criticized the community for months after he alleged repairs caused water damage and mold. Police say that, after Lambert killed Stuart and injured four others, he subsequently took his own life during a police standoff.

According to legal filings, Lambert had incurred damages topping $100,000 as a result of the HOA's "failure to take corrective action to remedy the moisture accumulation.".

Recent findings suggest that “No one should have to fear for their safety while doing their job or serving their community. Community association managers, building staff, and volunteer board members dedicate themselves to maintaining the places millions of Americans call home. They deserve to carry out those responsibilities without threats, harassment, intimidation, or violence,” the statement concludes.

Industry observers note that tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:24 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026.

LangChain Inc., a startup with a set of popular open-source tools for building artificial intelligence agents, has raised $300 million in funding.

Sources indicate that the Wall Street Journal reported today that Alphabet Inc.’s CapitalG fund led the round. It was joined by IVP, Sapphire Ventures, GIC and DFJ Growth. LangChain is now worth $3 billion.

Industry observers note that san Francisco-based LangChain is best known for the eponymous open-source framework it released in 2022. The software reduces the amount of work involved in building AI agents. LangChain makes it relatively simple to connect an AI agent to a large language model, integrate it with tools and add a system prompt. The framework also enables developers to customize details such as the format of prompt responses.

LangChain’s second open-source tool, LangGraph, is designed for situations where a task is too complicated to be automated by a single agent. LangGraph can link together multiple LangChain-powered agents into a single automation workflow. It can also add in other elements such as a mechanism that requires humans to approve sensitive actions.

In a recent development, the third component of LangChain’s open-source portfolio is Deep Agents. It extends LangChain and  LangGraph with features that make it easier for agents to perform complex work. There’s a virtual file system in which agents can keep data, a work planning tool and a subagent generation feature.

Sources indicate that langChain generates revenue with a suite of paid products called LangSmith. Developers can use it to not only build agents but also to maintain them once they’re in production.

Sources indicate that an AI agent usually goes through multiple iterations before it’s released to owners. LangSmith enables software teams to save those iterations in a centralized repository. If an update introduces a bug into an agent’s code base, developers can use LangSmith to promptly restore an earlier, bug-free version. Furthermore, they can compare the output quality of different agent versions to identify the one that should be deployed to production.

LangSmith also includes a set of observability features. It generates traces, logs that describe every single step of the workflow through an agent processed a prompt. LangSmith analyzes those traces to find technical challenges. From there, it prioritizes them based on their severity and generates code fixes.

It has been revealed that after its previous funding round last year, LangChain disclosed that its open-source tools were being downloaded about 90 million times per month. Its LangSmith suite, in turn, is used by Autodesk Inc., Cisco Systems Inc. and a long list of other tech firms.

LangChain reportedly intends to nearly double its headcount to 850 employees by the end of 2027. The company will hire infrastructure experts, AI engineers, salespeople and marketers.

  • According to recent reports, berkshire Hathaway revealed on Sept.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Billionaire investor Warren Buffett has officially stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway—marking the end of an extraordinary era for the 96-year-old businessman, whose approach to real estate has long been almost as unconventional as his investing career.

According to recent reports, berkshire Hathaway revealed on Sept. 18 that Buffett has been named chairman emeritus, effective immediately, while his son, Howard G. Buffett, has been elected chairman of the board. Buffett will remain a director and continue to offer his insight to the firm.

Sources indicate that “As Chairman Emeritus, Mr. Buffett will remain a member of the Board of Directors and will continue to offer his valued judgment and perspective,” Berkshire remarked.

The transition comes months after Buffett relinquished his CEO duties to longtime Berkshire executive Greg Abel, completing a carefully planned changing of the guard at the tech giant Buffett has been associated with since 1965.

Recent findings suggest that "I have served Berkshire since 1965," Buffett said in a letter to shareholders, released alongside the announcement. "Sixty-plus years in, I still have the best job in the world.".

Recent findings suggest that buffett isn't disappearing from Berkshire entirely. As chairman emeritus, he will remain on the firm's board, while Howard takes over as chairman and Abel continues running Berkshire as CEO.

"Serving as your Chairman has been the privilege of a lifetime, and I have never taken your trust for granted," Buffett wrote to shareholders while announcing the transition.

While Buffett's decades at Berkshire turned him into one of the wealthiest people on the planet, he has never amassed the sprawling collection of mansions and lavish vacation retreats often associated with billionaire status.

Instead, his property history is surprisingly limited—and anchored by the same Nebraska house he purchased nearly seven decades ago.

At the center of Buffett's real estate story is his longtime residence in Omaha, NE, which he purchased in 1958, when he was 28 years old.

Buffett paid just $31,500 for the five-bedroom property, which was built in 1921 and spans roughly 6,570 square feet. The home, where Buffett and his late wife, Susan Buffett, raised their three children, has remained his primary residence ever since.

Despite the enormous fortune he went on to accumulate, Buffett never traded the residence for a more extravagant billionaire compound.

The house has become closely associated with Buffett's famously restrained approach to spending, particularly when compared with the vast portfolios owned by many of his fellow billionaires.

The property is estimated to be worth about $1.44 million—a substantial increase from its 1958 purchase price, but still a relatively modest sum for a man whose fortune has climbed well into the billions.

Buffett has also made clear over the years that his attachment to the home goes beyond its financial value, repeatedly speaking about his satisfaction with the property rather than seeking out something larger or more luxurious.

Buffett's interest in properties began well before he purchased his Omaha residence.

As a teenager, the future billionaire used $1,200 of his savings to acquire a 40-acre Nebraska farm in 1944, making his first property investment at just 14 or 15 years old, depending on the timing of the purchase relative to his birthday.

Rather than working the land himself, Buffett arranged for a tenant farmer to operate it and split the proceeds—giving the budding investor an early lesson in owning an income-producing asset.

Decades later, he returned to farmland as an investment.

In 1986, Buffett paid $280,000 for a 400-acre Nebraska farm located north of Omaha, as per Architectural Digest.

The purchase further demonstrated his interest in land that could generate tangible, long-term returns rather than property acquired purely for status.

Buffett's land holdings extend beyond Nebraska and include farmland in Arizona and South Africa.

One of the biggest departures from Buffett's otherwise understated real estate history came in 1971, when he and Susan purchased a vacation home in the exclusive Emerald Bay community of Laguna Beach, CA.

They paid $150,000 for the property at a time when the surrounding area was far less developed than it is today.

Buffett later mentioned the decision wasn't driven by an investment strategy—he bought the home because his wife liked it.

Sources indicate that the three-level residence offered around 3,600 square feet of living space and six bedrooms, as well as a large deck with ocean views. Despite its coveted location, its interiors were relatively understated, with gray carpeting and white laminate kitchen countertops.

The property became a longtime family getaway, with Buffett and his family spending summers and Christmases there.

In a recent development, as the family expanded, so did their California footprint. Buffett acquired a neighboring residence to accommodate additional guests and connected the two properties with a staircase. He referred to the second house as the family's "annex.".

But Buffett's connection to the California retreat began to fade after Susan died in 2004.

He sold the neighboring property in 2005 and ultimately decided to part ways with the original vacation house as well.

Buffett initially put his Laguna Beach residence on the market for $11 million in 2017—46 years after paying $150,000 for it.

In a recent development, by August 2018, the asking price had been reduced to $7.9 million. The property ultimately sold for that amount later that year, according to previous reporting on Buffett's real estate holdings.

Even at the reduced figure, the deal represented a dramatic increase over Buffett's original purchase price.

It also left his property portfolio without one of its few traditional luxury homes.

The Laguna Beach residence stood in stark contrast to the Omaha house that Buffett has steadfastly held on to throughout his ascent from ambitious young investor to one of the most influential figures in American business.

Now, as he relinquishes the Berkshire chairmanship he held for more than five decades, that Omaha residence remains one of the most enduring constants of his life.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, artificial intelligence chipmaker Cerebras Systems Inc.
  • The company reported a loss before certain costs such as stock compensation of 67 cents per share, trailing Wall Street’s guidance of a 14-cent-per-share loss, though because of some accounting idiosyncrasies, its numbers are not directly comparable with that guidance.
  • The adjustments in Cerebras’ revenue are the result of some of the quirks in its accounting procedures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:40 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026.

In a recent development, artificial intelligence chipmaker Cerebras Systems Inc. delivered third-quarter revenue that comfortably beat expectations in its latest financial report today while announcing a new deal with Microsoft Corp., sending its stock up almost 18% in late trading.

The company reported a loss before certain costs such as stock compensation of 67 cents per share, trailing Wall Street’s guidance of a 14-cent-per-share loss, though because of some accounting idiosyncrasies, its numbers are not directly comparable with that guidance. Meanwhile, core adjusted revenue for the period came to $230.9 million, up 70% from a year earlier and surpassing the Street’s target of $214.7 million.

The adjustments in Cerebras’ revenue are the result of some of the quirks in its accounting procedures. The organization includes some pass-through revenue that’s subtracted from the total, and it also complications warrants to its major customers, which are then amortized as noncash reductions in revenue based on standard accounting rules, and so these are left out of the adjusted number.

Recent findings suggest that despite these complexities, investors were clearly impressed with the tech giant’s growth over the quarter, and perhaps even more so by its progress toward profitability. Though Cerebras has not been able to show a profit yet, its adjusted operating margin of -14% was still significantly better than its earlier guidance of -24% from three months earlier.

Chief Executive Andrew Feldman (pictured) told analysts on a conference call that the company has an advantage over its competitors, which are struggling to keep up with customer demand and dealing with growing order backlogs. “I think there is opportunity created, particularly on the hardware side, the sale of hardware, where long lead times in GPUs and more expense creates opportunity for us,” he noted, referring to Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units.

Cerebras does have a significant backlog for both hardware and cloud services itself, and that number rose from $25 billion in August to $26 billion at the end of the quarter. However, a significant portion of that backlog is related to the deal it struck with OpenAI Group PBC, Feldman said. This implies that other customers don’t have to wait so long for their orders to be processed.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the chipmaker continues to expand its customer base. After recently signing deals with Amazon Web Services Inc. and Oracle Corp., the tech giant today announced a latest customer in Microsoft Corp., although it didn’t provide many particulars about that agreement. The small increase in its backlog doesn’t do much to settle concerns that all of those deals are on the small side, however.

“We believe revenue begins to show up in quarter one of fiscal 2027,” Feldman remarked after explaining that the agreement with Microsoft was signed and sealed a month earlier.

Holger Mueller of Constellation Research said investors will have been pleased to see the growth in Cerebras’ cloud services business, which gives it a more dependable revenue stream than straightforward hardware sales. However, he also questioned the cost of that impressive growth.

According to recent reports, “Cloud and other services revenue was up 272% to $114.9 million, which is good, but the tech giant’s R&D expense more than tripled during the quarter to $177 million. That’s why its earnings-per-share loss more than doubled,” the analyst noted. “This is not sustainable over the long term, so Andrew Feldman is going to need to find a way to grow even faster, or else cut back on R&D spending in future. Investors will be watching closely to see what the longer-term plan for growth is.”.

Industry observers note that investor’s concerns over spending are valid, because Cerebras is likely to find it much harder to secure capital going forward due to the growing concerns around the sustainability of the broader AI infrastructure buildout. Feldman told analysts that the organization is now evaluating its financing options to find ways to meet customer demand and make inroads into its order backlog, but it’s not clear what that financing will look like.

Cerebras may perhaps be able to benefit from the uncertainty at its biggest rival Nvidia, which still dominates the AI chip industry, accounting for over 90% of all chip sales, according to some analysts.

Industry observers note that nvidia is in turmoil following the shocking resignation of its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang. It’s believed that Huang was likely forced to hand in his resignation after being outed for having an affair with an executive of a Singapore-based data center infrastructure firm, who is believed to have been acting as a spy for Chinese intelligence and a conduit for illegal shipments of GPUs into that country. Huang also had a second affair with one of Nvidia’s executives, according to reports that emerged yesterday, and reportedly a third one too.

Industry observers note that it may take a while for Cerebras and other chipmakers to take advantage of the disruption to Nvidia, which is seeking to maintain stability through the appointment of longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO, but in the short term its prospects still look good. The organization said it anticipates a core gross margin of 47% to 49% in the fourth quarter, with revenue rising to between $310 million and $330 million. Wall Street analysts are looking for a core gross margin of just 42.1% on sales of $271 million.

Moreover, Feldman told analysts on the call that the company believes its revenue will triple by the end of fiscal 2027. If that holds true, it would mean full-year revenue of around $2.85 billion, slightly below Wall Street’s long-term forecast of $2.92 billion in fiscal 2027.

Recent findings suggest that in 2026, Redfin added information about sunlight, weather, childcare access and more to home listings. Here is everything you need to know about what’s new.

It has been revealed that A home listing has always been good at telling you about a house: the square footage, the year it was built, the number of bedrooms. Historically, it has been less good at telling you what living there is actually like. Does the kitchen get morning sunlight? How hot are the summers? Is there a daycare within walking distance?

Sources indicate that those are the questions we set out to answer this year. Multiple newly introduced data sets arrived on Redfin in 2026, and they now sit alongside other information that was already there, including scores about a property’s walkability, transit access and climate.

Sunscore indicates exactly how much sunlight a home gets.

Recent findings suggest that natural light is one of the hardest things to judge from listing photos or a single showing, and it matters more than you might expect. In a recent Redfin survey, nearly 70% of people remarked the amount of sunlight in their home affects their satisfaction with where they live, and 11% said it is non-negotiable when searching for a home.

In a recent development, sunscore is a property-level rating from 0 to 100 that shows how much sunlight a home gets. We co-created it with Shadowmap, a sunlight analysis platform, using 3D modeling that tracks how shadows fall across a home throughout the day and across the seasons. Here are the score breakdowns:.

☀️ 90-100: Exceptional sunlight.

Each score accounts for the home’s 3D shape and structure, surrounding buildings, trees and terrain, the sun’s position throughout the day, and seasonal changes across the year. In other words, it catches the things you would only discover after moving in—like a neighboring building that blocks the afternoon light in winter.

And it is not only about comfort and aesthetics. A home’s sun exposure also says something about its solar potential, which can translate into real savings on energy costs over time.

Weather data helps predict precipitation and heat.

Recent findings suggest that weather turns out to be one of the biggest reasons people move. In a recent Redfin survey conducted by Ipsos, 22% of Americans planning to move to another state noted better weather was motivating the move—the most cited reason out of nearly 30 options, ahead of affordability, job opportunities and moving closer to family. Another 21% said concerns about climate change or natural disasters were shaping where they wanted to live.

In July, we partnered with The Weather Tech giant, owner of The Weather Channel app and weather.com, to bring historical weather data to every for-sale listing on Redfin. As our exclusive historical weather provider, it supplies the same data hundreds of millions of people check every month.

Each listing highlights ZIP code-level averages for:.

Consider this information the difference between the weather on the day you tour a home and the climate you might actually live in.

Childcare data displays daycare and preschool options.

It has been revealed that for families with young children, childcare access can determine a neighborhood’s fit as much as school boundaries do. However, it’s historically been missing from the home browsing experience. Redfin is the first major real estate portal to partner with Winnie, the largest marketplace for childcare and early education in the U.S., to bring local childcare information to for-sale listings.

Nearby daycare and preschool options now appear on for-sale home listings with details that determine whether a spot is realistic for your family, such as:.

Location scores capture everything from wellness access to noise.

While Walk Score, Bike Score and Transit Score already existed on home listings, Redfin has expanded these location scores to capture more information about a neighborhood’s vibe using Local Logic data.

Industry observers note that start exploring homes on Redfin.com or the Redfin app to learn everything you’d want to know about a property. Need a place to start? Use Redfin’s conversational search to begin your homebuying journey.

Kubernetes now runs containers and VMs side by side

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • KubeVirt’s graduation from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) marks a turning point in a debate that once pitted containers against virtual machines.
  • Enterprises still run much of their IT on VMs, even as AI pushes them toward newly introduced infrastructure.
  • According to recent reports, “But you’ve also got VMs, right, where you’re running applications in the old way that we did for decades before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 19:31 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026.

KubeVirt’s graduation from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) marks a turning point in a debate that once pitted containers against virtual machines. A decade on, Kubernetes is becoming one platform for legacy VMs, cloud-native apps and AI.

Enterprises still run much of their IT on VMs, even as AI pushes them toward newly introduced infrastructure. Red Hat Inc. is betting they won’t have to choose, with OpenShift 5 managing containers, VMs and AI workloads in one environment. Running two separate systems was never the goal, according to Fabian Deutsch (pictured), director of engineering for OpenShift Virtualization and Modernization and a KubeVirt maintainer at Red Hat.

According to recent reports, “But you’ve also got VMs, right, where you’re running applications in the old way that we did for decades before. And do you really want to maintain these two systems?” Deutsch said. “So our vision was, how can we unite those worlds to eventually make it easier to have one paradigm to run both, all these compute workloads on one platform.”.

According to recent reports, deutsch spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed KubeVirt’s graduation, running VMs and containers on one Kubernetes platform, AI’s influence on virtualization and what comes next for the project. (* Disclosure below.).

Recent findings suggest that kubernetes has drawn open-source projects and commercial providers onto a common platform, and AI’s hunger for compute has deepened that pull. Much of KubeVirt’s recent innovation now comes from the AI side, Deutsch explained.

Sources indicate that “You don’t want to repave your data center just because you’ve got a latest workload that you need to address,” Deutsch stated. “So you’re having that flexibility to run it in the way that you need it.”.

The CNCF announced the graduation at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, seven years after accepting the project into its sandbox. Next on the list is passing GPUs, CPUs and memory into VMs, while AI is changing how the community values virtualization itself, Deutsch noted.

“There’s a lot of influx of features due to AI, by the way,” Deutsch said. “The isolation model, we didn’t get to it in the beginning, but the isolation of virtualization is helping, right, in the AI age as well.”.

Sources indicate that the project already runs on edge devices and in the cloud because it offers a consistent API across those footprints, according to Deutsch. Nvidia Corp. was an early adopter, and Microsoft Corp. is now stepping up, he noted.

“I think it’s about getting the right and next generation infrastructure into your house,” Deutsch noted. “KubeVirt allows you to carry forward what you’ve got, what you invested in over the past decades, and not to leave it alone because you have to carry it forward.”.

Breaking: Fall Weddings Are More Popular Than Ever. Here's How to Dress for One (The Right Way)

📅 01 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved.
  • WEDDINGS CAN be hard to dress for, and this isn’t limited to those directly involved; being a mere attendant requires some degree of planning.
  • I covered some options for summer weddings a few months back, and just like that, we’re on to the next season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WEDDINGS CAN be hard to dress for, and this isn’t limited to those directly involved; being a mere attendant requires some degree of planning. I’ve attended quite a few weddings over the last year, both as a groomsman and as a regular guest, both with their own sartorial challenges. (I actually found it more stressful not being in the wedding party, at least in one aspect: I had to pick out my own outfit. This also allowed for a little creativity.).

I covered some options for summer weddings a few months back, and just like that, we’re on to the next season. Fall has arguably become the season for weddings; in fact, October recently overtook June as the most popular month for weddings in the U.S. I can attest to this; I was in two separate ones last October.

Summer and fall weddings have quite a few differences. You can get away with some more “fun” looks in the summer, and you can get a little more creative with the materials (linen, seersucker, etc.). Fall weddings are typically a little more buttoned-up, but there’s a little wiggle room there, too.

I’ll go through some of the easiest ways for guys to dress for an autumn affair—with different wedding types in mind—to get you off the ground. We also included plenty of price points because, as everyone knows, weddings can get expensive fast.

The Black Tux Essential True Navy Suit.

Brooks Brothers Explorer Collection Non-Iron Twill Button Down Collar.

Thomas Pink Classic Textured Solid Tie.

Cole Haan Men's Grand Neoclassic Plain Toe Oxfords.

We’ll start with what we consider a traditional wedding: a separate ceremony at a church, chapel, or the wedding venue without a black-tie dress code. This is about as classic as it gets, so you don’t have to go overboard—but we do recommend wearing a timeless suit. Our style team has tested plenty of affordable menswear brands offering solid options that approximate the look and fit of made-to-measure tailoring. One of them is the Black Tux, an upstart that offers suits for both rental and purchase, with virtual and in-person fittings to match you with the closest standard size. The prices are great, too: the Essential Suit is just under $300 all in. We also happened to score a 20 percent off code for the Black Tux, made exclusively for Men’s Health readers. Just use code MH20 at checkout (minimum of $295). The code’s good until October 31. Most of its higher-priced suits also include a rental option, but for the extra $100 or so, we’d recommend just buying one. The True Navy is a safe color you can wear year-round. The Grey Suit is a step up and is made from a heavier—but still breathable—merino wool. Perfect for the autumn temperatures.

A classic dress shirt is more than okay, but if you want to stand out in an otherwise pretty basic look, you can go with a classic twill dress shirt like this one from Brooks Brothers. You can get a little bit more creative with the tie, but nothing too crazy; the left-to-right diagonal stripes of a classic rep tie keep it distinguished. A Classic Textured Solid Tie is always a safe bet, too. Baby blue and pink go well with a gray suit, and navy, black, and red look better with gray. The shoes are easy, too: black plain-toe oxfords for grays, and these simple brown Astorflex Loafers with a crisp navy blue.

SuitShop Black Notch Lapel Tuxedo.

Brooks Brothers Classic Fit Double-Breasted Wool Pinstripe 1818 Suit.

Charles Tyrwhitt Non-Iron Twill Shirt.

Shinola Octagonal Onyx Inlay Cufflinks.

Charles Tyrwhitt Cotton Pocket Square - White.

Mack Weldon Silver Extended Crew Dress Sock.

The Black Tux Picture Frame Brushed Gold Tie Bar.

Recent findings suggest that black-tie affairs probably require even less creativity, but there are definitely ways to push the envelope to stand out. The safe choice, of course, is the classic tux. If you plan to need one on multiple occasions, we also love that the Black Tux once again gets top marks; its Essential option is also under $300. There are some pricier options you can also rent, but the Essential Tux is low-key enough to rock at any formal occasion. SuitShop is another upstart offering ready-to-wear tuxedos at accessible prices, including several options under $300. Accessories-wise, you can opt for a super fancy pair of onyx cufflinks from one of our favorite watch brands, Shinola, but something a little more budget-friendly is more than okay.

Industry observers note that nowadays, you don’t have to go all-black, at least depending on the event. But if you do deviate, you'd better make it count. Like upgrading to a double-breasted suit, for example. The Classic Fit Double-Breasted Wool Pinstripe 1818 Suit elevates your look without making you look like a Prohibition-era mobster (surprisingly, a very fine line).

The other major component of all of this: your shoes. You probably don’t want to go with a loafer; an oxford or derby shoe is the better option. Our favorite: Cole Haan’s Hawthorne Oxfords, a classic dress shoe that’s made with the brand’s famously comfortable insoles so your dogs will stay happy for hours. It’s also versatile enough to wear at dressy events or in a more casual office vibe. In other words, you’ll be getting a lot of use out of it.

It has been revealed that if you want to go all out, you can go full custom. Go big or go home, as they say. If you’re in the NYC area, Alan David Custom is a great choice. The bespoke tailor will give you a sample suit to try on before making final decisions, and the experience is a throwback to classier times. They’ll even ship it to you when it’s all said and done. If you want to go fully custom, you’ll also need the shoes to match.

Bonobos Empire Stretch Italian Wool Tuxedo.

Todd Snyder Italian Lightweight Sutton Jacket.

Quince Supima Cotton Herringbone Dress Shirt.

Todd Snyder Relaxed Fit Japanese Selvedge Chino.

Reigning Champ Stretch Chino Marina Standard Pant.

Allen Edmonds Rhett Cap-toe Oxford Dress Shoe.

Industry observers note that cocktail weddings give you a little more freedom than a traditional one. Here, you can rock a classic suit or a nice blazer and slacks, and you wouldn’t be wrong either way. The classic Ludlow tux from J.Crew gives off serious old-school cocktail jacket vibes, and it’s reserved for swankier occasions. Todd Snyder’s Italian Lightweight Sutton Jacket is another high-end option that’s both breathable and easy to wear throughout the night. If you wear blazers regularly, you’ll also get plenty of use out of this, even into the hotter months. Todd Snyder also makes our favorite pair of relaxed-fit chinos that check a lot of boxes for us. The Relaxed Fit Japanese Selvedge Chino is a steep departure from the ones we wear to the office, which is why it’s such a legit option for dressier occasions.

Industry observers note that if the baggier fit (and higher price tag) is scaring you off a bit, Reigning Champ makes an ultra-breathable cotton-twill chino that wears more like a standard dress pant. They’re comfortable, breathable, and have a little added stretch; you’ll get a lot of use out of them outside the wedding. The other big component of all of this: your shoes. You probably don’t want to go with a loafer; an Oxford or derby shoe is the better option. Our style team loves Allen Edmonds’. It’s made with calfskin leather, with a surprisingly light-yet-cushioned outsole that’s comfortable enough to use all night.

Billy Reid Exploded Glen Plaid Archie Jacket.

Abercrombie The A & F Collins Blazer.

Brooks Brothers Straight-Fit Cotton Advantage Chino Pants.

Brooks Brothers Friday Shirt, Oxford Patterns.

Madewell Johnny-Collar Sweater Polo in Slub Knit Cotton.

Cole Haan Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxford.

Barns have since had a huge come-up and are now a hugely popular wedding venue. Regardless of your stance on barn weddings, you have to dress a little differently. Vineyard weddings (and really any outdoor event) live in that same category. If you’re looking at a late-fall event, you’ll want something a little warmer. The Grey Plaid Wool Suit is a step up in that department without being too overbearing; the subtle designs also scream fall. You can also go with the blazer-and-dress-pants route. Abercrombie’s A&F Collins Blazer is a fantastic budget option, and the Olive Stripe colorway similarly gives off fall vibes. It’s easy to pair with dressier chinos, like the Straight-Fit Cotton Advantage Chino Pants from Brooks Brothers. They’re essentially dress pants with a certain chinoesque comfort.

Industry observers note that if you do go this route, you can have a little fun with the undershirt; Brooks Brothers’ Friday Shirt can add some flair to your getup. Madewell’s Johnny-Collar Sweater Polo is also a nice departure from your traditional button-down (and a lot more comfortable, too). If the wedding isn’t all that fancy, you can get away with rocking some of the most comfortable dress shoes/sneakers out there: Cole Haan’s Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxfords.

Buck Mason Capitola Linen Carry-On Jacket.

Todd Snyder Italian Linen Sutton Trouser.

Bonobos Stretch Weekday Warrior Dress Pants.

Reigning Champ Heavyweight Jersey OG T-Shirt.

In a recent development, the destination wedding can definitely be a challenge, depending on how close you are to the person (or people) getting married. They’re always a great time, though, and you can get similarly creative. We suggest a travel blazer; you’re already shelling out a lot of money for flights and accommodations, so you can save a few bucks by not checking a full suit. Our style director, Christian Gollayan, recently did a full review of the Bonobos Jetsetter Knit Blazer. He described it as a “lifesaver” when traveling. You can definitely rock it at a fall destination wedding, especially considering the hardworking knit construction. For a lighter, beachy vibe, Buck Mason’s Capitola Linen Carry-On Jacket is my own go-to. It holds its shape well for linen, and some of the darker colors work well for any season.

Pants are easy to pack, so we’d suggest going with something that helps you stand out. The Bonobos Stretch Weekday Warrior Dress Pants are the perfect counterpart to the Jetsetter, and you can wear them around the office when you’re not in wedding mode. The Italian Linen Sutton Trousers are a luxury pick, and the white colorway pairs particularly well with a navy blazer for a classic look. They’re also a lot easier to pack than regular dress pants. If the destination wedding is beach-themed, you can even get away with rocking a tee underneath your blazer. You don’t want to go with something too casual, and the Heavyweight Jersey OG T-Shirt from Reigning Champ is anything but. It’s well-made, fits like a glove, and is a great way to show off some jewelry if you like to wear a chain or two.

It has been revealed that ethereum developers want to upgrade the network to be quantum-ready by 2027, potentially accelerating one of its biggest security overhauls. Nasdaq-listed BTCS has been selling ETH below its purchase price to manage $64.1 million in outstanding Aave debt.

Both stories carry significant implications for Ethereum’s next growth phase. One could reshape its technical roadmap, while the other underscores the financial risks of treating ETH as collateral for aggressive DeFi strategies.

Ethereum research group Ethlabs wants developers to bring forward the network’s post-quantum security timeline to 2027. Its proposal, called pqai27, argues that advances in artificial intelligence are accelerating the risks surrounding quantum computing and existing cryptographic systems.

It has been revealed that the Ethereum quantum upgrade would aim to protect accounts, transactions, and network consensus against future quantum attacks. Ethlabs also wants Ethereum to become more resistant to AI-powered attacks that could expose vulnerabilities in its software.

The proposal comes two years ahead of the Ethereum Foundation’s existing December 2029 target for full post-quantum readiness. Google has separately targeted 2029 for its own post-quantum transition, while the U.S. government has moved its quantum security deadline from 2035 to 2030. Ethlabs wants two milestones achieved during 2027.

In a recent development, the first, called pqai-ready, would establish post-quantum consensus and give consumers a pathway toward quantum-resistant accounts. The second, pqai-scaled, would bring quantum-resistant transactions and data availability to full network capacity.

In a recent development, getting there requires developers to rethink upcoming network upgrades. Ethlabs has already offered to withdraw its Quick Slots proposal from the planned Hegotá hard fork to redirect resources toward quantum security.

It has been revealed that quick Slots would have reduced Ethereum’s block production interval from 12 seconds to 10 seconds. The group now wants to prioritize security and revisit faster block production in 2028.

Frame Transactions, meanwhile, remain central to the proposed transition. They would allow accounts to use more flexible authentication methods, including signatures designed to resist quantum attacks.

The Ethereum quantum upgrade could also change transaction economics, as Quantum-resistant signatures generally require more data, potentially increasing transaction costs and creating additional demands on wallet providers.

Recent findings suggest that ethlabs is effectively asking Ethereum developers to prioritize long-term security over certain performance improvements. This is a shift in priorities as the network competes for institutional adoption and real-world financial activity.

While Ethereum developers focus on future security, corporate ETH holders face a more immediate problem: leverage. BTCS disclosed in its latest quarterly filing that it sold ETH below its original purchase price to manage collateral levels and repay DeFi borrowings.

As of today, the Nasdaq-listed company had $64.1 million in outstanding Aave debt, including accrued interest. It backed that borrowing with 46,676 ETH valued at $99.3 million. That left its collateral worth 155% of outstanding debt. Based on those figures, the position carried an estimated liquidation threshold near $1,717 per ETH.

BTCS also reported $30.6 million in realized losses on digital asset transactions during the first nine months of 2026. The organization attributed the increase primarily to ETH sales used to manage collateral and repay DeFi borrowings, alongside accounting losses from depositing ETH into liquidity pools.

According to recent reports, the organization did not disclose how much ETH it sold below cost or how much of its realized losses came directly from those sales. But its borrowing history reveals the scale of the strategy. Between January 2025 and November 11, 2026, BTCS borrowed $152.4 million in stablecoins through Aave, primarily USDT and GHO. It repaid $89.4 million over the same period.

The company remarked no full or partial liquidation had occurred as of November 11.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the position illustrates the pressure that leveraged corporate treasury strategies can face when ETH prices fall. Borrowing against ETH creates additional capital opportunities, but declining collateral values can force companies to sell holdings or repay debt.

Inside Dolly Parton’s Eclectic Property Portfolio and Legacy As the Music Legend Receives Posthumous Grammy Nods

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dolly Parton has left behind a legacy that will continue to grow for years to come.

Recent findings suggest that the music legend—who passed away following a brief battle with cancer at the age of 80 on Aug. 25—was recently honored by the Recording Academy, receiving three posthumous nominations ahead of the 69th Annual Grammy Awards.

The "9 to 5" hitmaker has received two nominations in the Best Country/Duo Group Performance category for "Light of a Clear Blue Morning" with Lainey Wilson, Reba McEntire, Miley Cyrus, and Queen Latifah, and her "Butterfly" collaboration with the Zac Brown Band.

Parton's memoir, "Star of the Show: My Life on Stage," has also received a nod in the Best Audio Book, Narration, and Storytelling Recording category.

As Parton's contributions to the entertainment industry continue to receive their deserved recognition, it's worth noting another talent the country icon showcased throughout her lifetime: property investment.

To honor the country icon, Sept. 25 was hailed as "Dolly Parton day," and is set to be celebrated all across the country with parades, library fairs, community singing, and more.

Many hailed her on-stage talents, her generosity of spirit, and her philanthropic work—something that she demonstrated even through her love of property investment when she donated a longtime home to charity in 2023.

Parton's homes also provided her with a much-needed sanctuary, a place where she was able to retreat from the glare of the public spotlight and savor a private life at home with her husband, Carl Dean, who passed away in March 2025.

Indeed, despite her enormous celebrity profile, the "Jolene" singer still managed to keep her personal life at home largely hidden from the public, particularly when it came to the Brentwood, TN, estate she and Dean shared for years.

Parton also attempted to shield the public from her private health struggles—admitting earlier this year that she had neglected her own wellbeing while caring for Dean at the end of his life, but insisting that she was receiving the help she needed.

It was only revealed after news of her passing was revealed that she had been quietly battling cancer, although it is not known what type she had been diagnosed with.

Parton's death was shared in an Instagram post on her personal account, which featured a video filmed by her nephew Bryan Seaver.

"My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I’m representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis, and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next," he stated.

Industry observers note that "This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it til now.".

Industry observers note that he added: "Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy; he farmed the soil, she farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest.".

Seaver went on to praise his aunt as someone who "lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents, and countless others." He did not share a cause of death.

"A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family," an obituary shared with Realtor.com® reads.

"Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place.

"Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact.".

Hours after the news of her death was revealed, the late singer's family shared that she had spent her final days being treated for cancer.

“Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched. Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand," the statement read.

It continued, "“Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly’s unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact.

"After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones.".

Parton's death marks the end of an extraordinary life and career, one that also saw her build an impressive real estate empire that reflected her Tennessee roots and her superstar status.

Before she became a country music legend with a sprawling real estate portfolio, Parton was one of 12 children growing up in a tiny, rustic cabin tucked away in the Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee.

Parton spent her childhood in a one-bedroom cabin in Locust Ridge, which is situated just outside of Sevierville, TN, and had no electricity or running water, according to records.

Sources indicate that parton was born on Jan. 19, 1946 to Avie Lee Caroline and Robert Lee Parton Sr. in Pittman Center, TN. The songstress and her siblings, Willadeene, David, Coy, Robert Jr., Stella, Cassie, Randy, Larry, Floyd, and twins Freida and Rachel, all grew up in the humble home.

Although the property where she was raised is not available for fans to visit, they can gawk at a replica, which the country star recreated at her Dollywood theme park, which is located in Pigeon Forge, TN, and boasts “original treasures” from her early days.

The replica was constructed by Parton's brother, Bobby, and received a thumbs up from the country star's mom.

Sources indicate that outside, there is a sign that reads, “These mountains and my childhood home have a special place in my heart. They inspire my music and my life. I hope being here does the same for you! Dolly.”.

Although fans are not able to tour the grounds of the home where she was raised, they can still enjoy the city sights and view the statue of the country legend at the Sevier County Courthouse’s lawn.

In 2007, Parton and her husband purchased the two-bedroom, two-bathroom property for $1.2 million, but it never served as her main residence.

Sources indicate that she then listed the home for sale for $1.4 million in 2014—although records show that it only changed hands in 2023, when it sold for $1.2 million. It's unclear whether Parton quietly offloaded the home before its most recent sale.

Then, in July 2026, the property hit the rental market for $12,000 a month.

Built in 1923, the property sprawls across 1,091 square feet and offers guests a "rare opportunity to lease the legendary former home of Dolly Parton," per the listing, which is held by Richard Schulman of KW Westside Estates.

Situated in the heart of the city's Design District, the fully furnished home perfectly marries vintage charm with modern finishes while placing residents just steps away from Melrose Avenue, Santa Monica Boulevard, trendy restaurants, boutique shopping, and nightlife.

Upon entering the property, guests are greeted with an open floor plan that shows off the expansive living area and kitchen.

The living room boasts plenty of lounging space as well as a cozy fireplace for guests to enjoy on California's chilly evenings.

Moving into the chef's kitchen, there is wraparound marble counter that matches the patterned backsplash. The cuisine center also boasts state-of-the-art appliances.

"Inside, the open-concept living area is filled with natural light and stylish finishes, flowing into an updated kitchen with stainless steel appliances and designer tile," the listing notes.

The primary bedroom features enough room for a king bed and a seating area. It also boasts a glamorous walk-in closet, an en suite bath, and easy access to the lush backyard.

The second bedroom is just as charming thanks to its own private covered balcony. The property also boasts a humble laundry room, complete with seating areas.

Moving outside, there's a perfect entertaining area thanks to an open-air kitchen, a dining area, patio, and covered deck.

"Outdoor spaces include a tropical-inspired patio and covered deck ideal for dining and entertaining," reads the listing, which states that the property is available from Aug. 15, 2026.

The property's description also calls attention to the home's ideal proximity to many of Los Angeles' most interesting communities, stating: "This coveted neighborhood is known for its walkability, creative energy, and long-standing ties to entertainment and cultural history.".

Parton and Dean owned a mountainside sanctuary for decades before she decided to gift it over to the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Southern California, which offloaded it in July 2024, according to records.

The same month Dean passed away, the home was put back on the market for $770,000—just one year after it was sold for $585,00 by a charity that the musician donated it to in November 2023.

Just 30 days after being listed, the property was sold for above asking for $800,000.

Before being snapped up, the listing called attention to the singer, describing the home as "Dolly Parton's former Idyllwild retreat—a home as iconic as the legend herself.".

"If walls could sing, this charming three-story mountain retreat would be belting out a country classic," the description continues, noting that "nearly everything inside remains just as Dolly left it.".

Indeed, the property is filled with many of the personal items and collectibles that sat in the dwelling when Dolly last occupied the home, having used it as an escape for many years—although several modern updates have been made in the eight months since it last changed hands.

The listing noted that the home has been outfitted with a fresh luxury shingle roof, while an electric vehicle charger was also installed in order to add another layer of convenience, particularly given the home's rather remote location.

Still, the upcoming owners took pains to ensure that Parton's presence remains in every room, with the listing photos revealing that a tea set has been placed on the kitchen table, along with printed instructions addressed "to Dolly, from Steve," which detail how to make the perfect brew.

Elsewhere in the home, various knickknacks, including framed art, collectible plates, and various pieces of china can be seen adorning wooden shelves that run throughout many of the wood-paneled rooms.

A signed photo of Parton in her youth hangs on one of the walls, while one of the bathrooms has been outfitted with a guitar-shaped toilet seat for an added homage to her musical career.

Multiple fireplaces can be found in the living spaces and in the primary bedroom, adding a cozy feel to the 1,800-square-foot property.

Intriguingly, though the home now—quite literally—screams "Dolly Parton," her ownership of the property remained a closely guarded secret for many years and was only brought to light when it was sold in July 2024.

According to property records, the cabin was originally built in 1996, before being sold for just $126,000 in December 1994, which is when Parton is believed to have purchased it.

The "Jolene" hitmaker and Dean snapped up another quaint California house in 2004 and owned it for a decade, before quietly offloading it in 2014, when it sold for $940,000.

Located "in the heart of" the Danish-inspired town of Solvang, the adorable mini compound, which still retains many of the features added by the country music star during her ownership, features three petite properties: a main residence and two rental units.

"This one-of-a-kind property features the country legend's original, authentic 'Wig Room,'" state the listing for the home, which was being sold by its current owner, Chris Lapp.

A plaque stationed at the front of the dwelling proudly signals its impressive heritage as the "former home of Dolly Parton: singer, actress, and American icon," while a stained-glass window above the front door of the property's main residence features the legend's name, along with a butterfly.

However, one of the more eye-catching details at the front of the property has nothing to do with Parton at all, but rather pays tribute to Solvang's longstanding ties to Denmark and Europe: a miniature windmill that has been painted to match the home's distinctive gray, white, and red color palette.

Lapp, who bought the property in 2022 for $1.3 million, explained to SFGate that he'd heard Parton was inspired to purchase the dwelling because it "reminded her of her grandmother's home.".

Meanwhile, local resident and business owner Wes Leslie noted that the songstress may well have "hung on to" the dwelling as an "investment property," although he remarked it has also been rumored that she had family who used the home.

After he bought the home, Lapp spent a great amount of time restoring it to its original glory—and noted that he has ensured the tenants who at the moment live in the rental units have not made any significant changes to its interiors, many of which he believes were curated by Parton herself, including several heart stencils on the walls.

Beyond the special touches that Parton incorporated throughout the home, the property features a number of very unique features across all of its spaces: a three-bedroom, two-bathroom main house, a three-bedroom, two-bathroom rear unit, and a one-bedroom lower unit, all of which offer "private patios and off-street parking.".

Upon entry to the main residence, which has a cheerful red front door, visitors will find a bright, airy living room, a small, yet well-equipped kitchen, and three comfortable bedrooms.

The aforementioned "wig room" has been outfitted with an enormous mirror and a built-in vanity perfect for trying on different styles—however, a future occupant could easily use this space as a flex room or office.

Featuring large windows throughout, the property gets ample natural light—while the sun-soaked patio space provides another charming area for guests to relax and kick back.

For those eager to turn their next property investment into a lucrative business opportunity, the home's impressive history as a successful rental will no doubt be one of its most appealing features. According to the listing, it generated a "gross annual income of $116,000" via the rental units—which are both tenant-occupied.

Dean and Parton met on the day that she moved to Nashville when she was just 18 years old—bumping into one another outside of the Wishy Washy Laundromat, according to the Associated Press.

Two years later, the couple tied the knot in a heartfelt ceremony in Ringgold, GA, and opted to stay out of the spotlight, tucking away at their ultraprivate Nashville home where they lived throughout the entirety of their marriage.

The couple spent their days in a five-bathroom property that sits on 63 acres and is informally known as Willow Lake Plantation.

Although it's unknown how much the couple splashed out for the property, Realtor.com estimates that the property is now worth $8.8 million.

In 2014, Parton garnered approval from the Brentwood board to build a barn on the property that "architecturally matches" the other three barns on the residence and doesn't exceed 17 feet in height.

Because of the couple's bid for a private life, little is known about their two-story property.

Although Dean decided to remain out of the public eye, he frequently inspired his wife's career, most notably influencing her hit song "Jolene.".

In 2008, Parton told NPR that the song came to life after a bank teller developed a "terrible crush" on Dean.

"She got this terrible crush on my husband, and he just loved going to the bank because she paid him so much attention.

"It was kind of like a running joke between us when I was saying, ‘Hell, you’re spending a lot of time at the bank. I don’t believe we’ve got that kind of money.’ So it’s really an innocent song all around, but sounds like a dreadful one," she explained.

Their marriage has long been a hot topic as Dolly previously revealed that they have an emotionally "open marriage," and that she had even developed feelings for another man.

In 2017, Parton revealed in her book "Dolly on Dolly: Interviews and Encounters with Dolly Parton" that she developed crushes on other men while married.

"I've had crushes on some very unusual men, but Carl knows I'll always come home, and I'm not having sex with these people, I'm just flirting and having fun.

Recent findings suggest that "Yes, it's an open relationship, but not sexually, and I would kill him if I thought he was doing that.' He would shoot me too. At the end of the day, we love each other madly.

"I think so much of it is the fact that we are honest and open, and we have a warped sense of humor!" the singer explained while speaking to BBC.

Parton has also previously revealed that the couple opted to not have kids because she didn't believe "God" meant it for her.

"Since I had no kids, and my husband was pretty independent, I had freedom, so I think a major part of my whole success is the fact that I was free to work.".

Recent findings suggest that "I didn't have children because I believed that God didn't mean for me to have kids so everybody's kids could be mine, so I could do things like Imagination Library because if I hadn't had the freedom to work, I wouldn't have done all the things I've done. I wouldn't be in a position to do all of the things I'm doing now," Parton stated in a 2020 episode of "The Oprah Conversation".

She added that she has made "sacrifices" but is doing what she is "supposed to do.".

"I've made sacrifices, but I think, like I said, I believe what I know I'm supposed to do,” she said of her purpose.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:28 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026.

Q-CTRL Pty Ltd., a provider of quantum sensors and software for managing qubits, today confirmed that it has raised $290 million in funding.

It has been revealed that Q-CTRL sells a series of quantum navigation systems called Ironstone Opal. The manufacturer positions the product family as a more reliable alternative to GPS. Q-CTRL states that the devices can withstand jamming attempts, adverse weather and other challenging conditions that interfere with GPS signals.

Ironstone Opal tracks the host vehicle’s position with the help of sensors known as quantum magnetometers and quantum gravimeters. The sensors use variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and gravity as navigation cues.

Industry observers note that gravity is weaker at the top of a mountain than at sea level because the peak is farther away from the Earth’s core. The Earth’s magnetic field, in turn, exhibits perturbations at regions that have mineral deposits. Such gravitational and magnetic anomalies act as a unique fingerprint of the location where they occur. When a quantum sensor detects the fingerprint, it can deduce its location with relative ease.

Q-CTRL’s quantum magnetometers collect navigation data using tiny glass structures filled with clouds of atoms. The atoms change in specific ways when they encounter an anomaly in the Earth’s magnetic field. According to the manufacturer, its sensors detect those changes with the help of laser beams. Quantum gravimeters operate on a similar principle.

Recent findings suggest that ironstone Opal includes not only sensors but also software that processes the data they generate. It filters erroneous measurements, combines the remaining data with logs from other sensors and compares the information against pre-loaded maps.

Q-CTRL offers Ironstone Opal alongside a pair of software tools designed to make quantum computers easier to use. The first tool, Boulder Opal, helps researchers calibrate qubits in a manner that optimizes their performance. It’s complemented by Fire Opal, which makes quantum algorithms less prone to errors.

“The hard problem in quantum is not building the machine, it is getting useful output from it,” remarked Salesforce Ventures partner Robert Keith. “Q-CTRL solves that with AI-powered control software, and the proof is already public: a materials simulation on IBM hardware that any developer can now call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight.”.

Q-CTRL will use the proceeds from the funding round to enhance its software and grow its international presence.
